title: feat: support Meshtastic is_automation bit (#6449)
body:
Closes #6449.

Upstream meshtastic/protobufs#1134 reserves bit 2 (`0x04`) of `Data.bitfield` as `is_automation`: a bot or script sent the packet, not a person. Comment-only upstream change, so the wire format is the same.

## Changes
- **Outbound:** every automation-origin send (`SendOrigin: 'automation'`, #5414) sets bit 2. Manual sends leave `bitfield` absent, so their bytes don't change. No setting to turn it off.
- **Inbound:** migration 239 adds a nullable `messages.isAutomation` / `packet_log.is_automation` on all three databases. NULL means the bitfield was absent on the wire. Our own outbound rows store `true` for automation sends.
- **UI:** a `bot` icon on automation messages (channel, DM, Unified Messages) and an `is_automation` column plus detail field in Packet Monitor.
- **Automation Engine:** `trigger.message` gains `senderKind: 'any' | 'human' | 'automation'`. Absent means `any`, so existing rules don't change. The editor seeds `human` on new rules. MeshCore and Reticulum messages count as human. `trigger.isAutomation` is exposed as a token and a condition field.
- **Legacy Auto-Ack / Auto-Responder:** both skip flagged messages by default. A new per-source checkbox for each (`autoAckRespondToAutomation`, `autoResponderRespondToAutomation`) turns the skip off. The Auto-Ack converter maps that checkbox to `senderKind` (`any` when ticked, `human` when not).

## Mesh impact checklist
1. **Airtime:** none added. One bit on packets we already send.
2. **Spam:** less of it. The `human` defaults stop two MeshMonitor instances from replying to each other in a loop.
3. **Timers:** none added or changed.

## Not covered
- Admin packets carry no send origin, so they are never tagged.
- MQTT-native sends aren't tagged. Its NodeInfo beacon counts as the node's own broadcast, and its text sends are typed by a person.
- `mqtt_packet_log` already stores the raw bitfield, so it gets no new column.

## Testing
- Targeted Vitest suites for the builders, migration, repositories, manager skip logic, `triggerContext`, the Auto-Ack converter and parity tests, settings persistence, the public-instance sentinel audit, system backup tables, semantic tokens, and the UI rows all pass.
- Both `tsc` configs are clean and the lint ratchet passes.
- PostgreSQL and MySQL weren't running locally, so their tests skipped. CI is the first run on those backends.
- No screenshot yet. Packet Monitor has no render test.

title: fix(config): report when the node refuses an MQTT config save (#6439)
body:
Part of #6439.

## Summary

The reporter's RAK11200 runs firmware 2.7.21 or later, which is built with `MESHTASTIC_EXCLUDE_MQTT`. The node refuses every MQTT save and answers with a Routing `BAD_REQUEST` (32). MeshMonitor's save was fire-and-forget: it ignored that reply, showed "saved", and cached `enabled: true` until the next reload showed the node's real "disabled".

**The fix:**
- **`AdminTransactionService.sendLocalAdminAwaitRejection(payload, timeoutMs = 5000)`:** registers a waiter by packet id before sending, using the existing `sendAdminCommandAwaitAck` and `resolveByRequestId` correlation that `processRoutingErrorMessage` already feeds.
  - A non-zero routing error returns `{ rejected: code }`.
  - Silence, which is how a node accepts a local admin set, returns `{ rejected: null }` after the timeout.
  - The waiter is cleaned up on every path, and an unrelated reply can't settle it.
- **`DeviceAdminService.setMQTTConfig`:** waits for that result. On a refusal it throws `AdminConfigRejectedError` and does **not** update the cached config.
- **`POST /api/config/mqtt`:** a refusal returns `422 MQTT_CONFIG_REJECTED` with the message "The node refused this MQTT configuration. Its firmware may not include MQTT, or a setting is invalid." The UI shows it in the error toast and doesn't expect a reboot.
- **Checkbox fix:** after a reload, a missing `enabled`, `tlsEnabled`, `jsonEnabled` or `proxyToClientEnabled` now reads as off. Proto3 omits false values, so the boxes used to stay checked.

**Scope:** this covers the MQTT setter only. The generic module setters (serial, statusmessage and others) share a path with the read-back flow, so they're a follow-up.

**Side effect:** device restore calls `setMQTTConfig`, so a refused MQTT restore now fails instead of passing silently.

## Mesh impact checklist

This change sends no extra packets. The admin frame goes over the existing TCP link to the local node, not over the radio. On success, saving takes up to 5 seconds longer, because silence is the accept signal. It fires no notifications and arms no timers beyond that one wait.

## Tests

- `adminTransactionService.test.ts`:
  - a refusal is reported;
  - silence resolves after 5 s and the waiter is cleaned up;
  - an unrelated id is ignored;
  - a send failure cleans up the waiter.
- `deviceAdminService.test.ts`:
  - a refusal throws and leaves the cache untouched;
  - silence updates the cache.
- `configRoutes.mqttRejected.test.ts` (route harness): 422 on a refusal, 200 on accept, 500 on other errors.
- `ConfigurationTab.mqttRoundTrip.test.tsx`:
  - a missing `enabled` turns the checkbox off;
  - a refused save shows an error toast and no success toast.

All 106 tests pass. Typecheck is clean, and `lint:ci` has no in-repo FAILs.

title: fix(frontend): blank page — constants module touched Buffer in the browser
body:
## Summary

**`main` is broken:** the built app shows a blank page, with `ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined` in the browser console.

#6440 made the main frontend bundle import `src/server/constants/meshtastic.ts` for `PortNum`. That module built `MESHTASTIC_DEFAULT_KEY` with `Buffer.from()` at module scope, and browsers have no `Buffer`. Vitest and Node both define `Buffer`, so no test caught it; only a built bundle running in a browser fails.

**Fix:** the key is a real `Buffer` whenever `Buffer` exists, so server behaviour is unchanged. Otherwise it is a plain `Uint8Array`, which the browser never uses.

**Regression test:** `meshtastic.browserLoad.test.ts` loads the module with `Buffer` stubbed out, and checks that the server still gets a real `Buffer` with the right key. It fails on the old code.

Found during browser validation for #6444 and #6445.

## Mesh impact checklist

This change sends no packets, fires no notifications and arms no timers.

## Tests

- The `meshtastic` constants tests pass: 40 tests.
- Typecheck is clean.

title: fix(meshcore): raise source-connected/disconnected events for MeshCore sources (#6437)
body:
Fixes #6437.

## Summary

The automation `trigger.system` events `source-connected` and `source-disconnected` never fired for MeshCore sources. The engine builds them from the `connection:status` data event, but only `meshtasticManager` ever emitted that event.

**Fix:** `connectionState` in `meshcoreManager.ts` is now a private getter and setter. Every existing assignment already goes through the setter, which calls `dataEventEmitter.emitConnectionStatus({ connected, reason }, sourceId)`:
- **Edge-triggered:** a per-manager `lastEmittedConnected` flag means only transitions into or out of `connected` raise an event.
- **No retry spam:** a reconnect loop (reconnecting → connecting → reconnecting …) raises one `source-disconnected` and, once the link recovers, one `source-connected`. It never raises one per attempt.
- **User disconnect:** a `/disconnect` while connected raises one `source-disconnected`; while already down it raises none. The manager stays registered, as required by the MeshCore disconnect semantics.
- **Per source:** the flag is per manager instance, so sources do not affect each other. `nodeNum` is omitted; MeshCore has no numeric node id.

**Hung companions (the scenario in the issue):** a companion that hangs but keeps its transport open is only detected when the per-source **heartbeat** is enabled (`heartbeatIntervalSeconds`, off by default). After `heartbeatMaxFailures` probes fail (default 3), the manager calls `beginReconnect()`, which now raises `source-disconnected`.


## Also in this PR (maintainer decisions)

- **Companion heartbeat on by default, every 60 s.** This catches a hung companion that keeps its link open. The probe is a local `get_device_time` request over the TCP, serial or BLE link (meshcore.js command 5, reply 9) and sends nothing over the radio. With the defaults, three failed probes trigger a reconnect, so a hang is detected in about 3 minutes, and that reconnect raises `source-disconnected`.
  - New Companion sources start at 60 s: the Add Source form, the device-type reset and the env-created source (`COMPANION_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS` changes from 30 to 60).
  - The form now saves an explicit `0` for a Companion with the heartbeat off, so "off" can be told apart from "never set".
  - **Migration 238** (`meshcore_companion_default_heartbeat`, all three backends, idempotent) adds `heartbeatIntervalSeconds: 60` to existing Companion sources that have no stored value.
  - Explicit values (0, 30 and so on), Repeaters, other source types and unparseable configs are left alone.
  - The old form stored nothing when the heartbeat was off, so a source someone deliberately turned off before also gets 60 s; the maintainer accepted that. The change runs once, with no RF.
- **Automation editor note.** When a rule's trigger is `source-connected` or `source-disconnected`, a note next to the trigger fields recommends a cooldown of 10 minutes or more for rules that power-cycle or restart things. No default is imposed and not

title: fix(embed): honor public-instance mode in embed maps (#5156)
body:
Follow-up to #5156 (public-instance mode). Phase 3 (#6435) left embed maps out.

## Summary

Embeds are always served redacted: positions are snapped to ~1.5 km and timestamps are rounded down to the hour. The embed map didn't know this, so nodes in the same grid cell stacked on one point, and ages read oddly.

- **Server:** `GET /api/embed/:profileId/config` now returns `publicInstance: { enabled, hideLongNames, hidePublicKeys, roundTimestamps, hideMessageText }`. The values are booleans only, and the sentinel audit stays green.
- **`EmbedMap`**, when the mode is on:
  - Markers that share a coarse cell spread apart inside it, using the shared `applyPrecisionCellOffsets` at the 14-bit public cap. A lone marker stays centred.
  - Popup ages under an hour read "within the last hour" (`formatRelativeTime` `coarseHour`).
  - With the mode off, or from an older server that omits the field, nothing changes.
- **Not added:** the embed shows no message text, and no "public view" notice. The notice reads `AuthContext`, which the embed bundle doesn't provide, and a full-bleed embed has no spot for it.
- **Docs:** `embed-maps.md` gets a note, and the epic doc's "deferred: embeds" line is marked done.

Screenshots will follow in a comment.

## Mesh impact checklist

This change sends no packets, fires no notifications and arms no timers.

- `EmbedMap.test.tsx`: with the mode on, co-located nodes spread and show "within the last hour". With the mode off, or with the field absent, they are unchanged.

title: fix(meshcore-vn): show MeshMonitor's own channel sends as 0 hops, not "63 hops, 4-byte" (#6441)
body:
Fixes #6441

## Problem
A channel message sent from the MeshMonitor web UI was never received, so it has no `pathLen`. `encodeIncomingMessage` in the Virtual Node then fell back to `0xFF`, the fallback added in #3875. The MeshCore app reads that byte as width bits `11` (4-byte hashes) plus 63 hops. As a result, every message sent from MeshMonitor showed **"63 Hops - 4-byte"** in the app.

## Fix
- **`MeshCoreManager`** now tracks `sendPathHashSize`, the hop-hash width the node floods with:
  - When the device accepts `set_path_hash_mode`, it is the pushed default.
  - When the push is rejected or fails, it is the `path_hash_mode` the node reports in DeviceInfo (0–2 → 1–3 bytes). Firmware older than protocol v10 that reports no mode is treated as 1-byte.
  - It is cleared at the start of each `connect()`. Exposed as `getSendPathHashSize()`.
- On connect, the push is now **awaited** (was `void`) before the Virtual Node starts, so the width is known before the first relayed message. The push has a 5 s timeout so a device that never answers can't stall connect.
- **`MeshCoreVirtualNodeServer.encodeIncomingMessage`**: for an own channel send (`channel-N` marker in `toPublicKey`) with no `pathLen`, it sends `encodeOutPathLen(0, size)`. While the width is unknown it keeps `0xFF`. Received messages are unchanged.
- `getSendPathHashSize` is optional on the `MeshCoreVirtualNodeManager` interface. When it is missing, the width counts as unknown.

## Mesh impact checklist
1. **Airtime:** none. `set_path_hash_mode` was already sent on every connect. The fallback `device_query` runs only when that push fails, and both are local serial/TCP commands with no RF.
2. **Spam:** none. The change only affects the label byte in frames sent to Virtual Node clients.
3. **Timers:** none added.

## Tests
- `meshcoreVirtualNodeServer.test.ts`: an own send encodes to 0x00/0x40/0x80 for widths 1/2/3, and to 0xFF when the width is unknown. A received message with no `pathLen` stays 0xFF.
- `meshcoreManager.pathHashSize.test.ts`: the width is unknown by default, taken from the push when it succeeds, and falls back to DeviceInfo, then to pre-v10 → 1, then to unknown. The existing assertions are updated for the new timeout argument.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` is clean, and `lint:ci` shows no in-repo FAIL lines.
- Full Vitest run (PG/MySQL containers not running, so those suites skipped): 37,223 passed, 55 failed.
  - All 55 failures are in `takV2Decoder.test.ts` and `linkPreviewRoutes.test.ts`, which this change doesn't touch.
  - They fail the same way on the base commit, because of this sandbox (dependencies installed with `--ignore-scripts`, no outbound network). CI is the authority.

-- Authored by Roger 🤓

title: fix(virtual-node): stop blocking waypoints from virtual node clients
body:
## Summary

The Virtual Node has a list of port numbers it blocks from connected apps when admin commands are not allowed, which is the default. Since the Virtual Node was added (`ed7e956eb`), that list has been `[6, 8]`:
- 6 is ADMIN_APP, which is correct.
- 8 was commented as NODEINFO_APP, but 8 is **WAYPOINT_APP**. NodeInfo is 4.

As a result, apps on a Virtual Node could not send waypoints, and NodeInfo, which the comment meant to block, was never blocked. This came up in the review of #6440.

Maintainer decision: block **neither** of them. Only ADMIN_APP stays blocked.

## Changes

- **`src/server/virtualNodeServer.ts`:**
  - `BLOCKED_PORTNUMS` is now `[PortNum.ADMIN_APP]`.
  - The `adminPayload && portnum === ADMIN_APP` check drops the now-redundant portnum test.
  - The `else` comment now says what that branch is: an admin packet with no payload, which is still blocked.
  - ADMIN_APP handling is otherwise unchanged:
    - the addContact guard (#1487);
    - the localhost and self-addressed rules;
    - favorite/unfavorite interception;
    - removeByNodenum ack-and-drop.
- **New `virtualNodeServer.blockedPortnums.test.ts`:** drives the real `handleClientMessage` from a remote client with admin commands off.
  - A WAYPOINT_APP packet is forwarded to the radio.
  - A NODEINFO_APP packet is forwarded to the radio.
  - An ADMIN_APP packet is still blocked.
- **`virtualNodeServer.test.ts`:**
  - Removed the "Admin Command Filtering" block, which re-implemented the logic locally and called port 8 NODEINFO.
  - The config-state tests now use NodeInfo = 4.

## Mesh impact checklist

1. **Airtime:** a waypoint from a Virtual Node app becomes one mesh packet. It is sent only when a person sends one from their app, the same as a text message from that app, and nothing sends them automatically. NodeInfo behaviour does not change; it was never blocked.
2. **Spam and feedback loops:** none added. Nothing in MeshMonitor reacts to a client's waypoint by sending something.
3. **Timers:** none.

## Tests

- 109 tests in 8 `virtualNodeServer*` files pass.
- Typecheck is clean.
- `lint:ci` has no in-repo FAILs.

title: refactor: use PortNum constants for port numbers and ban bare ones in lint
body:
## Summary

CLAUDE.md says to use the shared `PortNum` constants and never bare port numbers. Production code used `PortNum.*` 129 times but still had about 33 bare numbers. This PR replaces them and adds a lint rule so new ones fail `lint:ci`.

There is no behaviour change; every value is the same.

### Replaced
- `src/utils/packetFormat.ts`: the 20 `case N:` lines in `getPortnumColor`.
- `src/server/virtualNodeServer.ts`:
  - three `=== 6` (ADMIN_APP) checks;
  - the `=== 1` that #6438 just added;
  - `BLOCKED_PORTNUMS`.
- `messageContentFilter.ts`, `useMessagingView.ts`, `MessagesTab.tsx`, `useWebSocket.ts`, `ChannelsTab.tsx`, `DmMessageRow.tsx`, and `App.tsx` (the send payload).
- `mqttPacketFilter.ts` has `portnum: 0`, which is a drop-counter starting value, not a port number. It keeps the literal with a reasoned `eslint-disable`.

### Lint rule (`eslint.config.mjs`, `no-restricted-syntax`)
The rule matches names like `portnum`, `port_num`, `normalizedPortNum` or `msg?.portnum`. It flags:
- such a name compared to a numeric literal (`===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`);
- a `switch` on such a name with numeric `case` labels;
- an object literal of the form `{ portnum: <number> }`.

The existing raw-SQL selectors moved into a shared `SQL_BAN_SELECTORS` constant. That way the components/pages block and a new `src/test/**` / `**/test-helpers/**` block keep the SQL ban: a later `no-restricted-syntax` block replaces earlier ones rather than adding to them. Tests, fixtures and migrations are exempt from the port-number rule.

Both rules were checked on scratch files:
- **Port-number rule:** it fired on each pattern above, and did not fire on `msg.channel === 1` or `{portnum: undefined}`.
- **Raw-SQL ban:** it still fired on `db.prepare`.
- **Components block:** a component file got both the port-number error and the `fetch()` error.

## Found, not changed: `BLOCKED_PORTNUMS` blocks WAYPOINT_APP, not NODEINFO_APP

The comment calls port `8` NODEINFO_APP, but 8 is WAYPOINT_APP; NodeInfo is 4. This has been the case since the Virtual Node was first added (`ed7e956eb`). With admin commands off, which is the default, Virtual Node apps cannot send waypoints, and NodeInfo was never blocked.

This PR keeps the value 8 and adds a NOTE. Whether to fix it is a separate decision.

## Mesh impact checklist

This change sends no packets, fires no notifications and arms no timers. It is a constant swap plus a lint rule.

## Tests

- `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- `lint:ci` has no in-repo FAILs. The baseline is unchanged; I did not run `lint:baseline`.
- 34 test files with 346 tests passed. They cover packetFormat, messageContentFilter, virtualNodeServer*, useWebSocket, useMessagingView, MessagesTab, ChannelsTab, DmMessageRow, mqttPacketFilter and App. The full suite runs in CI.

title: fix(virtual-node): relay text messages from one client to the other connected clients (#6436)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #6436. When several apps share a Meshtastic Virtual Node (Android app, `contact`, `termtastic`), a message sent from one app reached the web UI and the mesh but never showed up in the other apps. Messages sent from the web UI already reached every app.

### Root cause
`VirtualNodeServer.handleClientMessage` stores the client's outgoing packet by calling `processIncomingData(..., { skipVirtualNodeBroadcast: true })`. That flag is there so the packet isn't relayed back as an echo, but it also stops the packet reaching **every other** client. Web-UI sends go through `sendTextMessage`, which relays the message to all clients on its own path, so only app-to-app traffic was affected.

### Fix
- `broadcastToClients(data, excludeClientId?)` takes an optional client to skip.
- After the outgoing packet is stored, a `TEXT_MESSAGE_APP` packet (replies and reactions included) is relayed to the other clients, skipping the sender so its app doesn't show the message twice. The `from` field is filled in the same way as for the stored copy (Android sends `from=0`, #626).
- Other packet types (position, telemetry, admin and so on) are not relayed. That matches the web-UI path, which only relays text.

**Known limit:** a DM that the client PKI-encrypts itself has no `decoded` portnum, so it is not relayed. Channel messages and plain DMs are.

## Mesh impact checklist
1. **Airtime:** none. The relay is a local TCP write to apps on the virtual node. Each packet is still forwarded to the physical node exactly once, as before.
2. **Spam / feedback loops:** the receiving apps only display the `FromRadio` packet and never re-send it. The relay doesn't touch `dataEventEmitter`, notifications or automations, because `processIncomingData` already ran exactly once, as before. The sender is excluded, so there's no echo.
3. **Timers:** none added.

## Tests
- New `src/server/virtualNodeServer.clientMirror.test.ts`:
  - a text message reaches the other clients but not the sender, and is still queued for the physical node;
  - non-text packets are not relayed;
  - `broadcastToClients` with no exclusion still reaches every client.
  - The first test fails without the fix and passes with it.
- All `virtualNodeServer*` suites pass (113 tests). `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` is clean, and `lint:ci` reports no in-repo FAILs.
- Full local Vitest run: 6 failures, all in `src/server/routes/linkPreviewRoutes.test.ts`. That file doesn't touch this change; the failures look like the sandbox blocking outbound URL lookups. PostgreSQL/MySQL suites were skipped (no containers), but there are no schema changes. CI is the authority here.

-- Authored by Roger 🤓

title: feat(privacy): public-instance mode phase 3 — UI for redacted views, docs (#5156)
body:
Closes #5156. This is Phase 3 of 3 of public-instance mode, after #6433 (redactor and middleware) and #6434 (leak audit). The plan and notes are in `docs/internal/dev-notes/PUBLIC_INSTANCE_MODE_EPIC.md`.

## What this does

The UI now handles redacted data for signed-out viewers:
- **Names:** the long name falls back to the short name, then the node id (`getUserDisplayName`). This covers the node list, messages, popups, search, the header and MeshCore views.
- **Hidden message text** shows as an italic placeholder, never as raw text. This includes DM list previews.
- **Times:** a relative time rounded down to the hour reads "within the last hour".
- **Maps:** coarse positions are drawn as approximate on both map surfaces. With accuracy regions on, they show ~1.5 km accuracy cells. MeshCore markers that share a cell are spread apart.
- **Notice:** a one-line "Public view" notice appears on the node list and the message views.
- **Exports:** server-side export buttons are hidden, since those exports are blocked for signed-out viewers.
- **MeshCore:** signed-out contact views no longer request data with the truncated key.
- **CoT warning:** Settings warns when the CoT/TAK feed is on together with public-instance mode, because that feed is not redacted.

The frontend learns it is redacted from `/api/auth/status`. Signed-out replies carry a `publicInstance` object; signed-in replies don't.

## Login blocker fixed (from Phase 1, never released)

Browser validation found that with the mode on, nobody could sign in. The redactor treated the 64-hex CSRF token as a MeshCore key and cut it to 12 characters, so every login failed with `CSRF_TOKEN_INVALID`.

The fix:
- `/csrf-token` and `/auth/*` are now skipped by the middleware. They carry no mesh data.
- A new `opaqueTokens` catalogue class never alters values under token, challenge or nonce keys.
- An end-to-end test turns the mode on, signs out, fetches the CSRF token and logs in. Without the fix, it fails.

No release tag contains Phase 1.

## Docs

- New page: `docs/features/public-instance-mode.md`, with a sidebar entry.
- Cross-links from the privacy disclosures, ATAK (CoT caveat), embed maps and settings pages.
- `CLAUDE.md` gains a hard rule: new response fields must match the redaction catalogue, or the sentinel audit fails.

These come from an isolated container with a fresh volume and no devices or MQTT, filled with made-up data. Nothing was sent.

@@ -0,0 +1,100 @@
+# Public-Instance Mode
+
+*Added in 4.16.0.*
+
+Limit what strangers can see on a MeshMonitor you open to the public.
+
+If signed-out visitors can read your dashboard, they can read node names, exact positions,
+message text, and public keys. Public-instance mode removes or blurs that data before it
+leaves the server. It applies to every signed-out viewer and to embed maps.
+
+Signed-in users never see redacted data, whatever their role.
+
+## Turn it on
+
+Open **Settings** and find **Public-instance mode** (`settings-public-instance`).
+The master switch starts off. Turn it on, then pick what to hide.
+
+| Setting | Default | What it does |
+|---|---|---|
+| Public-instance mode (master switch) | Off | Nothing below applies until you turn this on. |
+| Hide long names | On | Removes long names. Short name and node ID stay. |
+| Hide public keys | On | Cuts MeshCore keys to a 12-hex prefix and removes Meshtastic keys. |
+| Round times down to the hour | On | Rounds timestamps down to the hour. |
+| Hide message text | On | Replaces message text with a placeholder. |
+
+The four toggles only matter once the master switch is on. Each starts on, so switching
+the master on gives you the strictest setup.
+
+## Always on
+
+These rules apply whenever the master switch is on. You cannot turn them off.
+
+| Data | What a signed-out viewer sees |
+|---|---|
+| Positions | Snapped to a grid of about 1.5 km. If a node already reports a coarser precision, that coarser value stays. |
+| Distances | Rounded to 1.5 km. |
+| Bearings | Rounded to 10 degrees. |
+| Altitudes | Rounded to 100 m. |
+| Raw packet payloads | Dropped. |
+| CSV, NDJSON, and file exports | Blocked. The server answers `403` with code `PUBLIC_INSTANCE_UNSUPPORTED_RESPONSE`. |
+
+## What each toggle changes
+
+**Hide long names.** Long names become empty. Short names and node IDs stay, so people can
+still tell nodes apart. A sender name inside MeshCore channel text goes too, unless message
+text is also hidden.
+
+**Hide public keys.** MeshCore keys keep their first 12 hex characters. Meshtastic keys are
+removed, along with key-fragment details from key-security checks.
+
+**Round times down to the hour.** Last-heard times, message times, and similar fields drop
+to the start of the hour.
+
+**Hide message text.** Message text becomes `[hidden on this public instance]`. Mesh waypoint
+names and descriptions get the same placeholder, since mesh users write them.
+
+## What stays visible
+
+- Map markers you create as the operator.
+- GeoJSON layers and map styles.
+- Short names, node IDs, and device roles.
+
+## What it does not cover
+
+- **The CoT/TAK feed.** The TCP feed sends exact positions to anyone who connects. Settings
+  shows a warning when both the feed and public-instance mode are on. See
+  [ATAK / CoT Integration](./atak#phase-3-cot-feed-atak-wintak-network-input).
+- **The `/api/v1` token API.** Token holders are not signed-out viewers, so the mode skips
+  them. Issue tokens only to people you trust with exact data.
+
+## Related controls
+
+Public-instance mode changes what signed-out viewers see. It does not decide whether they
+can see a source, channel, or page at all.
+
+- **Anonymous-user permissions.** To hide data entirely, take read access away from the
+  anonymous user. Public-instance mode then has nothing left to redact for that data.
+- **`ok_to_mqtt` filter.** A separate per-source setting (#6393) hides a node, and its data,
+  from signed-out viewers when the node reached you over MQTT with `ok_to_mqtt` off and was
+  never heard directly over RF on that source. It works with or without public-instance mode.
+- **Embed maps.** [Embed maps](./embed-maps) always count as signed-out, even if a signed-in
+  user opens the page that hosts them.
+
+Pair this with your [Privacy Disclosures](./privacy-disclosures) so visitors know what you
+show and what you hide.
+
+## For developers
+
+The server redacts API responses by field name. The catalogue lives in
+`PUBLIC_INSTANCE_FIELD_CATALOGUE` in `src/server/utils/publicInstanceRedactor.ts`. The
+middleware in `src/server/middleware/publicInstanceRedaction.ts` applies it to every
+response for a signed-out viewer.
+
+- A new field that carries a position, name, key, text, or timestamp must match the
+  catalogue. Fix leaks in the catalogue, with a unit test, not in one route.
+- `src/server/routes/publicInstance.sentinelAudit.test.ts` walks every `GET` route as a
+  signed-out viewer and fails if a seeded sentinel value leaks. New routes need no setup;
+  edit the table file only for routes the defaults cannot call.
+- Frontend code must handle null long names and null keys. Use `getUserDisplayName`.
+- Design notes: `docs/internal/dev-notes/PUBLIC_INSTANCE_MODE_EPIC.md`.

title: test(privacy): public-instance mode phase 2 — sentinel audit of every anonymous route (#5156)
body:
Part of #5156. This is Phase 2 of 3 of public-instance mode, after #6433. The plan is in `docs/internal/dev-notes/PUBLIC_INSTANCE_MODE_EPIC.md`.

## What this does

Adds a **sentinel audit**. The test fills the database with unique marker values across Meshtastic, MeshCore (companion and MQTT ingest), Reticulum, MQTT and embeds. It turns public-instance mode on with every toggle, grants the anonymous account every permission, then calls **every GET route** on the API router and the embed router while signed out. The run fails if any marker appears in a response body or header. It also replays each toggle on its own, so a leak that only shows when one toggle is on is caught too.

A new route is covered automatically because the test walks the real router. Exceptions are listed only when needed: `SKIP`, `EXPECT_ERROR`, `ROUTE_OVERRIDES`. Minimum data floors per protocol (overall 80; MT 45, MC 25, RNS 8, MQTT 3, embed 3) stop a broken fixture from passing by returning 404s.

## Changes

- **`createApiRouter`** (`src/server/routes/apiRouter.ts`): the API router setup moved out of `server.ts` unchanged, so the audit can mount the exact production stack. The mount order is identical; the before and after lists of 86 mounts were checked equal during the refactor. Guard tests check that `server.ts` adds no mounts outside the factory, that the `/api` mounts match an allow-list, that the embed mount stays redacted, and that redaction is the first handler.
- **Leaks the audit found, all fixed in the redactor catalogue, with no route code changed:**
  - Name fields the catalogue didn't know: `from_node_longName`, `fromNodeName`/`toNodeName`, `localName`, `node_name`.
  - Mesh waypoint `name` and `description` are now hidden with message text. Operator-made map markers stay visible, like GeoJSON layers.
  - `keySecurityIssueDetails` carried an 8-character key fragment; it is now nulled.
  - Position-estimate uncertainty is rounded to the nearest 1.5 km.
  - Values inside maps keyed by node id or channel are now caught: estimate uncertainty and first-unread times. The MeshCore snapshot `seqCursor` (a max timestamp) is rounded too.
  - MeshCore channel text stored as `Name: body` had the sender's name in it. The prefix is now stripped when long names are hidden and message text is shown.
- No exact coordinates, public keys or raw payloads leaked. A test route added on purpose to return a marker was caught by the audit.

## Mesh impact checklist

This change sends no packets, fires no notifications and arms no timers. It is a test, a router refactor, and redactor catalogue entries.

## Tests

- The audit file has 14 tests and runs in about 6 s. It calls 326 routes, 83 of which return seeded data.
- Locally:
  - Typecheck and `lint:ci` are clean.
  - The targeted run passed 979 tests across 230 suites, with none failing or skipped. It covered the audit, redactor, middleware, signed-in vs anonymous, `apiRouter`, public-surfaces, settings persistence, and the sourc

title: feat(privacy): public-instance mode, phase 1: settings, redactor, middleware (#5156)
body:
Part of #5156. This is Phase 1 of 3 of public-instance mode; the plan is in `docs/internal/dev-notes/PUBLIC_INSTANCE_MODE_EPIC.md`.

## What this does

Adds a global **Public-instance mode** setting under Settings, off by default. When it is on, signed-out visitors and public embeds see less detail. Signed-in users see everything, as before.

When the mode is on, signed-out viewers get these changes. The first three are fixed and cannot be turned off:
- **Positions** snap to a ~1.5 km grid (Meshtastic `precision_bits` 14). A position the node already sends at a coarser precision is snapped to its own grid, so it does not change.
- **Distance, bearing and altitude** round to 1.5 km, 10° and 100 m. Without this, they could be combined to work out the exact position again.
- **Raw packet payloads** (hex, bytes) are dropped.

These four are each a separate toggle and default to on:
- Hide long names. The short name and node id stay.
- Hide public keys. Meshtastic PKI keys are removed. MeshCore keys are cut to their 12-hex id prefix, the same way everywhere, so the client can still join records.
- Round timestamps down to the hour.
- Replace message text with a placeholder.

## How it works

- **One response redactor** (`publicInstanceRedaction`) is the first handler on the API router and also wraps the embed router. It decides when the response is sent, after per-route auth has run.
  - **JSON:** it walks every JSON body and redacts by field name, using a data catalogue (`PUBLIC_INSTANCE_FIELD_CATALOGUE`). Any route that returns JSON is covered, including routes nobody touched.
  - **Other content types:** images, fonts, tiles, CSS and JS pass. Operator-authored GeoJSON and map styles are marked exempt. Anything else, such as the CSV/NDJSON exports, is **blocked** for signed-out viewers because it cannot be redacted by field name.
- **Failure handling** fails closed:
  - If redaction throws, the viewer gets a 503 and never the original body.
  - If the setting cannot be read, a signed-out viewer gets the same 503.
- Numeric strings, which is how PostgreSQL and MySQL return BIGINT values, are redacted the same as numbers.
- `/api/v1` (API-token routes) is not touched.
- The setting is loaded before the server starts listening, and reloaded on save and on reset.

Out of scope: the CoT/TAK feed is not redacted. Phase 3 adds a Settings warning for it.

## Mesh impact checklist

This change sends no packets, fires no notifications and arms no timers. It only changes what HTTP responses contain.

## Tests

- `publicInstanceRedactor.test.ts`: covers every field class, numeric strings, the precision rules, inputs that must not change, and the error path.
- `publicInstanceRedaction.test.ts`: uses the route harness to cover anonymous, signed-in, mode off, v1, embeds, the content-type allow-list, streaming, the 503 paths and `Vary`.
- `publicInstance.signedInVsAnonymous.test.ts`: uses the **real** `/api/nodes`, `/api/poll` and `/api/messages/channel/0` routes.

+|---|---|
+| Scope | One global setting, default **off**. Not per source. |
+| Positions | Always coarsened when the mode is on: snap to a ~1.5 km grid (Meshtastic `precision_bits` 14). A position that is already coarser passes unchanged. |

+  user and trimmed for an anonymous one; typecheck, lint:ci and the suite are green.
+- [ ] **Phase 2 — Sentinel audit.** A route-walk test over every mount in

+  responses for the sentinels. Fix every leak it finds in the redactor's field
+  catalogue (not per route). Exit: the audit is green, and a new GET route that

title: fix(meshcore): parse the repeater 'get name' replies the console actually sends
body:
## What breaks

A MeshCore **repeater source over direct serial** shows up as `Unknown Repeater` in the node list and in `/api/sources/:id/nodes` even though the device reports a proper name to `get name`:

```
POST /api/sources/<id>/meshcore/cli  {"command":"get name"}
→ {"success":true,"data":{"reply":"-> > LT-KM Seniava 44","elapsedMs":9}}
```

while the node row for the same source is:

```json
{"nodeId":"mc:<source>:repeater","publicKey":"repeater","longName":"Unknown Repeater","shortName":"Unkn"}
```

Because the name is wrong, anything derived from it is wrong too: the HA/MQTT name, the local-node row in the UI, and the label used when the manager reports the device.

## Why

`refreshLocalNode()` parses the CLI reply with a single hard-coded shape:

```ts
// Repeater CLI returns "  -> > DeviceName" format
const nameMatch = nameResponse.match(/->\s*>\s*(.+)/);
…
name: nameMatch ? nameMatch[1].trim() : 'Unknown Repeater',
```

The serial console is interactive, so the same value arrives in more than one shape depending on the firmware build and on how far the console has got through its boot:

```
  -> > LT-KM Seniava 44     two prompt markers (the shape the regex expects)
  -> LT-KM Seniava 44       one prompt marker
LT-KM Seniava 44            no prompt
  -> Unknown command        console not ready yet (or unsupported verb)
get name                    the command echo
```

Anything that is not the two-prompt form falls through to `Unknown Repeater`. That is reproducible right after a power cycle or USB re-plug: the first `get name` of the connection is answered with `Unknown command` (or only one prompt marker), the name is lost, and it stays lost until a later refresh happens to catch a two-prompt reply.

## Fix

- New `src/utils/meshcoreRepeaterName.ts` — `parseRepeaterNameResponse()` turns a `get name` reply into the name or `null`:
  - splits on CR/LF, strips repeated `->` / `>` prompt markers,
  - drops the echoed `get name`, bare prompts, and `Unknown command`,
  - unwraps one pair of surrounding quotes,
  - returns the last usable line.
- `refreshLocalNode()` uses it, and when the reply yields nothing it asks `get name` once more after a 2 s pause before falling back to the placeholder — the booting-console case, without adding a retry loop.

No behaviour change for a reply that already matched the old regex.

## Tests

`src/utils/meshcoreRepeaterName.test.ts` — 10 cases: both prompt shapes, no prompt, echoed command, `Unknown command`, bare prompt after the value, quoted name, empty/whitespace reply, `null`/`undefined`, and a name that legitimately contains `>`.

```
npx vitest run --pool=threads src/utils/meshcoreRepeaterName.test.ts
 ✓ |unit| src/utils/meshcoreRepeaterName.test.ts (10 tests)

npx tsc -p tsconfig.server.json --noEmit   # clean
npx eslint src/utils/meshcoreRepeaterName.ts src/utils/meshcoreRepeaterName.test.ts   # clean
```

## Mesh impact

None. This only classifies the reply to a local serial CLI command that `co

title: build(deps): bump satellite.js from 7.1.0 to 7.2.0
body:
Bumps [satellite.js](https://github.com/shashwatak/satellite-js) from 7.1.0 to 7.2.0.
Release notes

Sourced from satellite.js's releases.

7.2.0

Highlights

  • json2satrec keeps microseconds of epoch instead of truncating them.
  • New alpha5ToNumber function to decode Alpha-5 form into a number.
  • New eciToEcfVelocity function which returns a true ECF velocity (with the Earth's rotation removed) and its inverse. In contrast, eciToEcf when applied to velocity only rotates axes without accounting for Earth's rotation.
  • Fixes to eciToGeodetic and invjday precision.
  • Multiple fixes to WASM, and performance improvements.

Full changelog

  • Fix: json2satrec kept only the milliseconds of the OMM EPOCH, dropping up to 999 µs of a microsecond epoch; the digits beyond the millisecond are now carried into epochdays.
  • Feature: add alpha5ToNumber to convert a TLE catalog number field to a number, decoding the Alpha-5 form used above 99999 (A0000 = 100000, Z9999 = 339999, I and O skipped). twoline2satrec is unchanged and still returns satnum as written.
  • Feature: add eciToEcfVelocity(positionEci, velocityEci, gmst), which returns a true ECF velocity: the ECI velocity rotated into ECF axes with the Earth's rotation (ω × r) removed, and its inverse ecfToEciVelocity(positionEcf, velocityEcf, gmst). eciToEcf and ecfToEci only rotate the axes. Note that dopplerFactor keeps expecting the rotated-only velocity from eciToEcf(velocityEci, gmst) in 7.x and compensates for the observer's rotation itself; passing it the true ECF velocity puts the range rate off by up to ω·R·cos(latitude), about 0.46 km/s at the equator. The next major version switches dopplerFactor and the bulk EcfVelocityCalculator to the true ECF velocity (#180).
  • Fix: eciToGeodetic returned a height of about -6400 km for a point on the rotation axis (its R / cos(latitude) term collapses there) and was metres off within a millimetre of it. The height is now R cos(lat) + z sin(lat) - a / C, which is exact at the poles. The WASM GeodeticPositionCalculator kernel gets the same change.
  • Fix: invjday truncated the fractional second instead of rounding it, so invjday(jday(date)) came back a full second early for about half of all inputs that fall exactly on a second, and the array overload could report sec = -1. invjday now

title: feat(admin): verified remote config saves that read the setting back (#4487)
body:
Closes #4487 (the re-query part left open after #4502).

## What
A **Verify config saves** checkbox on the Admin Commands tab, shown when a remote node is selected. When it's on, each remote `set*Config` save runs as a background job:

1. Send once.
2. Wait 90 s for the node to settle (most sections reboot on save).
3. Read the section back with `get_config_request` / `get_module_config_request`.
4. Resend **only** when the read-back shows a changed field still holding its old value.

A **Verified saves** panel lists running and recent jobs (status, sends, checks, stuck fields) and has a Cancel button. Routes: `GET /api/admin/verify-jobs` and `POST /api/admin/verify-jobs/:id/cancel` (admin only).

## How a check is judged
The job compares three things: the decoded packet it actually sent, the snapshot loaded before the save, and the read-back. Only fields the save changed are judged.
- **Read-back = sent** → applied.
- **Read-back = old value** → not applied → resend.
- **Neither** → the firmware rewrote it (clamp or boot-time coercion) → settles as `differs`, no resend.
- **No reply** → schedules another read and **never** resends. On an asymmetric link (the node hears us, we can't hear it), resending would reboot-loop the node.
- **A resend answered with the same stuck fields** → stops as `refused`. Firmware floors look exactly like a lost packet: `node_info_broadcast_secs` < 3600, `neighbor_info` < 4 h, and a remote LoRa config the node judges invalid (it reverts the whole section and still ACKs). Without this guard, those would reboot the node up to 5 times.
- **Fields that 2.8 redacts on remote gets** (`network.wifiPsk`, `mqtt.password`) are skipped. Security saves are refused (keys don't read back).
- **No snapshot loaded** → `409 VERIFY_NEEDS_BASELINE` ("Load this config from the node first").

## Mesh impact
- **Airtime:** a check is one get request + reply (~2 packets, about 8 transmissions at 3 hops; getters need no passkey). A resend is the set packet. Worst case per job is about 24 checks plus 5 sends over 2 h.
- **Spam / loops:** opt-in only. Resends need a read-back that proves the old value. A repeated identical result stops the job. One job per node + section (a new save replaces the old job), 3 per source (`429 VERIFY_JOB_LIMIT`).
- **Timers:** jobs are in memory (same as `adminOperationService`). A restart drops them; it never re-fires a send. Settings saves don't touch them.
- Limits chosen by the maintainer: checks every 5 min (first at 90 s), give up after 2 h or 5 sends, re-check only on timeout, 1 job per node / 3 per source.

## Tests
- `adminVerifyJobService.test.ts`: comparator, diff, target resolution, job lifecycle with fake timers (verified / no-reply never resends / resend then verify / refused / differs / fatal / cancel / replace / cap).
- `adminRoutes.verifyJobs.test.ts`: route harness covering 202, baseline 409, unsupported 400, 429 cap, admin-only.
- `VerifyJobsPanel.test.tsx`.
- Affected suites: 49 files / 777 t

title: fix(virtual-node): forward NodeDB flags so Android 2.8 shows the right lock and link (#5921)
body:
Closes #5921

## Cause
The Virtual Node builds each NodeInfo from the MeshMonitor DB, which has never stored NodeInfo fields 12–15. The Meshtastic expert checked Android v2.8.3 (`NodeSecurityIndicator.kt`, `NodeManagerImpl.kt:844-855`, `Capabilities.kt:143`, `NodeItem.kt:466-480`):

- **Wrong lock:** `signsPackets` comes only from `has_xeddsa_signed` (14), and every NodeInfo overwrites it. When the field is missing, 2.8 peers drop from SIGNED_NODE to the plain public-key lock.
- **"Broken link":** this is the orange `SignalOff` "unheard on current LoRa" badge, not a link icon. When the radio reports firmware 2.8.1 or newer, the app reads `heard_on_current_lora` (15). The Virtual Node passes the radio's 2.8.1 version through but never sent field 15. The field decodes as false, so every node without MQTT gets the badge.

## Fix
- `MeshtasticManager` caches `is_key_manually_verified`, `is_muted`, `has_xeddsa_signed` and `heard_on_current_lora` from the radio's NodeDB replay, in memory. The radio replays them on every connect, and the cache is cleared with `deviceNodeNums`. New method: `getDeviceNodeFlags()`.
- `createNodeInfo` encodes the four fields, and `sendNodeInfosFromDb` sends them.
- If the radio did not list a node (it is in the DB only), it is marked heard on LoRa unless it came via MQTT. This avoids a badge on nodes this source heard over RF.

## Mesh impact
None. No new packets, timers or notifications. Only the replay sent to Virtual Node clients changes.

## Tests
- Protobuf round trip of the four fields.
- Manager caches the flags from `processNodeInfoProtobuf`.
- Virtual Node replay: a listed node passes its flags through, an unlisted RF node counts as heard, and an MQTT node does not.

Not checked on hardware with an Android 2.8.3 client.

title: feat(meshcore): re-join Room Sync rooms with a blank-password ACL login (#6408)
body:
Closes #6408

## What

A MeshCore room server keeps an ACL. A blank-password login from a key already in it gets back in with its old permission (`simple_room_server/MyMesh.cpp`: `if (data[8] == 0) client = acl.getClient(...)`). This PR uses that so Room Sync works without a saved password, and re-joins rooms after a restart.

- **"Joined" is recorded, no secret stored.** Migration 237 adds `meshcore_nodes.lastRoomLoginOkAt` (epoch ms of the last *successful* room login from this source; all three backends). `lastRoomSyncAt` could not serve: the scheduler stamps it on every attempt, failed ones too (#5036). The stamp is written from `MeshCoreManager.loginToNodeWithRetry`, the one path every login takes, so Rooms UI, remote console and Room Sync logins all count. Contacts known not to be rooms are skipped.
- **Blank fallback.** For rooms with Room Sync on and `lastRoomLoginOkAt` set, the scheduler logs in with a blank password when nothing is saved. A saved password still wins. A room with neither is skipped instead of blocking the rooms behind it (before, it sat at the head of the overdue queue and the tick returned early).
- **Re-join on connect.** No separate burst. After a source connects (startup or reconnect), each joined room is due once on the normal tick, so the existing one-login-per-source-per-60s floor (`getLastMeshTxAt`/`recordMeshTx`) still holds. A room is skipped when its last persisted login (`max(lastRoomSyncAt, lastRoomLoginOkAt)`) is under 60 minutes old. A room ruled out at connect stays settled for that connection, so the restart never becomes the trigger later on.
- **Interval counts interactive logins too.** `isRoomSyncEligible` now measures from `max(lastRoomSyncAt, lastRoomLoginOkAt)`, so the scheduler does not log in again minutes after the user did.
- **Same failure rules.** 0x86 refusal disables auto-sync at once; no reply counts towards `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES = 3`, then disables. Receive-only sources skip (existing first-statement guard).
- **UI.** For a room with no saved password and a recorded failure, the login card now says: "This room server no longer lets this radio back in without a password, so auto-sync has been turned off. Log in again with the password." (or the unanswered variant). The alert icon tooltip no longer says "saved password" when none is saved.

## Mesh impact checklist

**1. Airtime.** One login is up to 3 sends (`MESHCORE_LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS`). A refusal stops after 1. When the room's path is unknown each send floods, so roughly 4-8 transmissions per send across the mesh; with a known path it is a direct send. Bounds:
- At most **one login per source per 60s** (existing per-source TX floor, also counted for failures).
- Startup / reconnect re-join: **one try per joined room per connection**, and **none if any login to that room was persisted within the last 60 minutes**.
- Steady state is unchanged: one login per room per configured interval (min 60 min).
- Worst case for N joined rooms aft

title: fix(automation): MT↔MC bridge relays the operator's own MeshCore channel posts (#6409)
body:
Fixes #6409.

## Problem
Channel messages the operator sends on the bridged MeshCore node never reach Meshtastic through the MT↔MC Bridge. This happens even though the bridge sets `includeSelf: true` (#4694 / #4695).

## Root cause
MeshCore stores channel messages differently depending on direction:
- **Received** channel post: `fromPublicKey = 'channel-<idx>'`
- **Outgoing** (own) channel post (`sendMessage` / `sendChannelMessageAs`): `fromPublicKey = <our pubkey>`, `toPublicKey = 'channel-<idx>'`

The automation engine read the channel index from `fromPublicKey` only (`parseMeshCoreChannelIdx`). Our own channel posts therefore came out as `isDM = true` with no channel. The bridge's `isDM == 0` condition and its MeshCore channel filter both rejected them.

## Fix
- New `meshCoreMessageChannelIdx(msg)` in `triggerContext.ts`. It tries `fromPublicKey` first and falls back to `toPublicKey`. It replaces the four call sites that only looked at `fromPublicKey`: the context builder, the matcher, the miss-describer and `onMeshCoreMessage`. A received DM's `toPublicKey` is our real key, not a `channel-` slot, so DMs are still classified as DMs.
- Before the fix, an own send stored with the `'local'` placeholder key (local node key not known yet) was classed as a DM. With the fix it is now a channel post, so a channel autoresponder could react to it. To prevent that, `onMeshCoreMessage` now treats `fromPublicKey === 'local'` as self-origin for every message. Before, only reactions got this check. Rules without `includeSelf` keep ignoring our own sends.

## Mesh impact checklist
1. **Airtime:** no new periodic or per-node traffic. The bridge now relays one message per operator-typed MeshCore channel post. That is the behaviour #4694 meant to deliver, and the existing per-rule rate limit (default 20/min) still applies.
2. **Spam / loops:** the bridge's own relayed sends now also arrive as self-origin channel messages. They carry the `MT@` tag, so the existing `notContains 'MT@'/'MC@'` loop guard drops them (covered by `bridge.loopSafety.test.ts`). Every other automation still drops self-origin through the #3914 guard, which now also covers the `'local'` placeholder.
3. **Timers:** none touched.

## Tests
- New unit tests in `triggerContext.test.ts`:
  - an own outgoing channel post becomes a channel message, not a DM, and matches by channel index and channel name
  - a received DM stays a DM
- New engine tests in `automationEngineService.test.ts`:
  - an `includeSelf` channel-filtered rule fires on an own outgoing post and resolves the channel name from the `toPublicKey` slot
  - a `'local'`-keyed send is self-origin
- `src/server/services/automation` + `src/components/automations`: 2616/2616 pass. `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` is clean, and `lint:ci` reports no in-repo failures.
- Full `src/server` run: 55 failures, all in `takV2Decoder.test.ts` and `linkPreviewRoutes.test.ts`. They fail the same way on the base commit without this change, so they come fro

title: fix(meshcore): pair neighbour directions by freshness on the maps (#6403)
body:
Fixes #6403

## Problem
When both repeaters of a pair list each other in `meshcore_neighbor_info`:
- **MeshCore map** (`MeshCoreMap.tsx`) drew **two overlapping polylines**, one per direction, each with its own sticky tooltip. The tooltip you saw on hover belonged to whichever line rendered on top, and that depended on API row order.
- **Dashboard map** (`DashboardMap.tsx`) used `dedupByUnorderedPair`, which keeps the **first** row per pair, so the line's SNR-driven opacity also depended on row order.

The neighbour fetch deletes and re-inserts a repeater's rows, so the order changed on every refresh and the shown SNR flipped between a stale entry (12.75 dB, heard ~12 h ago) and the current one (-10.25 dB, heard 4 min ago).

## Fix
- New `pairNeighborRecords()` in `src/utils/neighborLinks.ts` (pure, no Leaflet). It groups directed records by unordered pair, keeps the freshest record per direction (`timestamp - lastHeardSecs*1000`; a known age beats an unknown one; ties are broken by key so row order never matters), makes the fresher direction `primary`, and attaches the other one as `reverse`.
- **MeshCoreMap** now draws one line per pair. The tooltip shows both directions with their age, freshest first, for example:
  `KH_HOLODOS_R1 hears Merefa_R1: -10.3 dB (4 min ago) · Merefa_R1 hears KH_HOLODOS_R1: 12.8 dB (12 h ago)`
- **DashboardMap** sets opacity from the freshest direction instead of the first row.

Not in scope: hiding or dimming stale directions past an age cutoff. That needs a threshold, which is a policy choice for the maintainer. The Map Analysis `MeshCoreNeighborLinksLayer` still draws one line per row; it has its own time-window filter and inspector, and can move onto the same helper later if wanted.

## Mesh impact
None. This only changes how the frontend renders existing data. It sends no packets, fires no notifications and arms no timers.

## Tests
- `src/utils/neighborLinks.test.ts`: freshest-wins, independence from row order, the fetch timestamp is taken into account, known age beats unknown, duplicate directions, `neighborHeardAtMs`, `formatNeighborAge`.
- `src/components/MeshCore/MeshCoreMap.neighborPairs.test.tsx`: one line per pair and the tooltip text, with the issue's data in both row orders, plus the single-direction case.
- Ran locally: `neighborLinks`, `DashboardMap`, and all of `src/components/MeshCore/` passed (1729 tests). One suite, `meshcoreResponderMatch`, failed to collect because the native `re2` module was not built (`npm ci --ignore-scripts`). That is an environment issue unrelated to this change. `tsc --noEmit` is clean and `lint:ci` reports no in-repo failures.

-- Authored by Roger 🤓

title: feat(meshcore): embedded MeshCore MQTT broker source with upstream forwarding (#6197)
body:
Closes #6197.

New source type `meshcore_mqtt_broker`: an embedded MQTT broker (Aedes) that MeshCore observers publish to directly. Frames feed the existing MeshCore MQTT ingest (`decodeObserverPacketMessage`), so Packet Monitor, node discovery, channel decryption and observer stats work with no new decode code. Implements the binding decisions in the issue's last comment.

## Decisions → implementation
1. **Source type.** `MeshCoreMqttBrokerManager` subclasses `MeshCoreMqttManager` and only swaps the transport. Read gates that used the `'meshcore_mqtt'` string now call a predicate (`isMeshCoreMqttFedSourceType` / `isMeshCoreMqttBrokerManager`). No TX or device gate changed.
2. **Auth.**
   - Token login: username `v1_{PUBKEY}`, token verified with `verifyAuthToken` (signature + expiry), audience must match, key must be on the allowlist.
   - Static username/password login: compared with `timingSafeEqual`.
   - **The allowlist binds every login.** A static login may publish only under allowlisted keys; any other key is dropped as `not_allowlisted`.
   - Anonymous logins and MeshMonitor's own forwarding key are refused.
3. **Topics.** Only `meshcore/{IATA}/{PUBKEY}/packets` and `/status`. A token login publishes only under its own key, and the body `origin_id` must match the topic key. All subscribes are refused and nothing is retained.
4. **Limits** (defaults, admin-adjustable up to ceilings of 1,000 / 200 msg/s / 1 MB):
   - 50 observers, refused at login over the cap.
   - 20 msg/s per connection; excess is dropped and counted, and the session stays open.
   - 64 KB payload. A socket that announces a packet far over the cap is cut.
5. **Diagnostics** on the source's Overview tab and a count badge on the sidebar card. Per connection: last topic, last reject reason, counters. The last 25 refused logins and disconnects. Needs `nodes:read` on the source; IPs, upstream URLs and listener errors also need `sources:read`.
6. **Upstream forwarding.** Off by default, opt-in per target, forwards only that target's allowlisted observers, with an optional IATA filter.
   - **Pass-through:** original topic and body, with the target's username/password.
   - **Own identity:** republished under a MeshMonitor observer key with a minted, auto-renewed token. Observers' status is not relayed here, because one observer going offline would mark the whole identity offline. The target publishes MeshMonitor's own online status with an offline last will instead.
   - A target stops reconnecting after 5 rejected logins.
   - Loop guard: forward clients never subscribe, our own key can't log in, a target can't point at our own port, and a payload we forwarded in the last 120 s is dropped if it comes back.
   - A privacy warning sits next to the forwarding section and on each enabled target.
7. **Not in v1:** WebSocket listener, one-click Analyzer Observer link.

**Storage.** No migration. The own-identity key reuses `meshcore_observer_keys`, keyed by the broker source id;

--- docs/features/meshcore-mqtt-broker.md (+151/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,151 @@
+# MeshCore MQTT Broker
+
+::: tip Added in 4.18 (#6197)
+Run an MQTT broker inside MeshMonitor that MeshCore observers publish to directly. No external broker to stand up.
+:::
+
+## What it is
+
+A `meshcore_mqtt_broker` source listens for MQTT connections from MeshCore observers (repeaters and Companion observers that publish in the Analyzer format). Frames they publish feed the same pipeline as a [MeshCore MQTT Ingest](/features/meshcore-mqtt-ingest) source, so you get the Packet Monitor, node discovery from adverts, channel decrypt (for keys you hold) and observer battery / uptime with no extra setup.
+
+It is the MeshCore twin of the Meshtastic [Embedded MQTT Broker](/features/mqtt-broker).
+
+**This source has no radio.** It never transmits on RF. Load is capped by the limits below, and the optional forwarding is MQTT only.
+
+Use it when you want a private, local observer network. To read a public region feed instead, use [MeshCore MQTT Ingest](/features/meshcore-mqtt-ingest). To publish what your own Companion hears to a public broker, use the [Analyzer Observer](/features/meshcore-analyzer-observer).
+
+## Setting one up
+
+**Dashboard → Add source → MeshCore MQTT broker.**
+
+| Field | Notes |
+|---|---|
+| Listener port | TCP port observers connect to. Default `1884`. Must not clash with another broker source. Expose it from the container (`-p 1884:1884`). |
+| Allowed regions | Optional IATA codes. Blank accepts any well-formed code. |
+| Token audience | The audience observers sign their token for. Blank turns token logins off. |
+| Allowed observer public keys | One 64-hex key per line. Binds every login: a token login needs a key on this list, and a static login may only publish under keys on it. |
+| Static username / password | Optional fixed login, for observers that use one. |
+| Limits | Max observers (default 50), messages per second per connection (default 20), max payload (default 64 KB). |
+| Upstream forwarding | Optional. Off by default. See below. |
+
+Anonymous logins are always refused. A config with neither a token audience nor a static login cannot be saved.
+
+WebSocket listeners are not in v1. Observers must use plain MQTT over TCP.
+
+## Authentication
+
+Two ways in:
+
+1. **Observer token.** Username `v1_{PUBKEY}` (the observer's 64-hex public key), password the Ed25519 token the observer mints. MeshMonitor verifies the signature, the expiry, and that the token's audience matches the one you set. The key must be on the allowlist.
+2. **Static login.** The username and password you set. Any observer that knows them can connect, but it may only publish under keys on the allowlist.
+
+A token login may only publish under its own key: the `{PUBKEY}` in the topic must match the key it logged in with. A static login may publish under any allowlisted key; a frame under any other key is dropped and counted, and the session stays open.
+
+## Topics
+
+```
+meshcore/{IATA}/{PUBKEY}/packets
+meshcore/{IATA}/{PUBKEY}/status
+```
+
+- `{IATA}`: 2 to 8 letters or digits (`test` works). Checked against the allowed regions when you set any.
+- `{PUBKEY}`: the publishing observer's 64-hex public key. The body's `origin_id` must match it.
+
+Observers cannot subscribe. The broker refuses every SUBSCRIBE, so one observer can never read another's raw feed, and nothing is retained.
+
+## Payload format
+
+The broker accepts the format the MeshCore Analyzer bridge publishes. Only `raw` and `origin_id` are required for a packet; every structural field is re-derived from `raw`. `type`, when present, must be `PACKET`. (Keys and `raw` are shortened below.)
+
+A `packets` message:
+
+```json
+{
+  "origin": "Hilltop Repeater",
+  "origin_id": "3F2A9C...64 hex characters...B71E",
+  "timestamp": "2026-11-14T18:22:05.118Z",
+  "type": "PACKET",
+  "direction": "rx",
+  "packet_type": "4",
+  "route": "F",
+  "len": "38",
+  "payload_len": "32",
+  "raw": "1100A1B2C3D4E5F6...",
+  "SNR": "7.25",
+  "RSSI": "-92",
+  "hash": "9C4E1A2B3D4F5A6B"
+}
+```
+
+A `status` message (observers usually publish it retained, every few minutes, plus an `offline` last will):
+
+```json
+{
+  "status": "online",
+  "timestamp": "2026-11-14T18:20:00.000Z",
+  "origin": "Hilltop Repeater",
+  "origin_id": "3F2A9C...64 hex characters...B71E",
+  "model": "Heltec V3",
+  "firmware_version": "1.9.1",
+  "radio": "915.0,250.0,10,5",
+  "client_version": "meshcoretomqtt/1.0",
+  "stats": { "battery_mv": 4105, "uptime_secs": 86400, "noise_floor": -112 }
+}
+```
+
+## Diagnostics
+
+The source's page (**Overview** tab) shows a **Broker connections** card:
+
+- each connected observer: login kind, accepted / dropped counts, **last topic**, **last reject reason**;
+- recent login refusals and disconnects;
+- forwarding target state (connected, sent, dropped, last error).
+
+Reject reasons you will see:
+
+| Reason | Meaning |
+|---|---|
+| Login refused (bad or missing credentials) | Wrong static password, anonymous login, or a username that is neither the static one nor `v1_{PUBKEY}`. |
+| Login refused (key not on the allowlist) | Valid-looking token login from a key you have not allowed. |
+| Login refused (token invalid or expired) / (audience does not match) | The token failed verification. |
+| Login refused (observer limit reached) | Max observers reached. |
+| Dropped (over the message rate) | More than the per-connection msg/s limit. The observer stays connected. |
+| Dropped (payload too large) | Over the payload cap. A connection that announces a packet far over the cap is cut. |
+| Dropped (key not on the allowlist) | A static login published under a key you have not allowed. |
+| Dropped (region not allowed) | IATA segment malformed or not on the allowed list. |
+| Dropped (key in topic, token and origin_id differ) | Topic key differs from the login key or from `origin_id`. |
+| Dropped (raw is missing) / (type is not PACKET) / (origin_id is not 64 hex characters) / (raw is not a MeshCore frame) | Body problems. |
+| Dropped (our own forwarded frame came back) | The loop guard caught a frame MeshMonitor forwarded. |
+
+These counters live in memory and reset when the broker restarts.
+
+Who sees what: the card needs the same per-source **Nodes: read** permission as the rest of the page. Observer IP addresses, upstream URLs and listener errors also need **Sources: read**.
+
+## Upstream forwarding
+
+Off by default, and opt-in per target. Each target forwards only the observers you list on it (packets and status), with an optional IATA filter. An empty observer list forwards nothing.
+
+::: warning Observer data leaves MeshMonitor
+Forwarding sends your observers' frames to the broker you name. Only add a target you trust with that data, and list only observers whose owners agreed.
+:::
+
+Each target picks an identity:
+
+| Mode | What upstream sees | Login | Notes |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| **Pass-through** | The original topic and body, verbatim | The target's static username / password | Keeps per-observer attribution. Token-only brokers (LetsMesh) refuse it. |
+| **Own identity** | Every frame under MeshMonitor's own observer key; `origin_id` and `origin` rewritten | A token MeshMonitor mints for the target's audience | Works with LetsMesh. All frames appear to come from one observer. |
+
+Own identity needs a MeshMonitor observer key. Edit the saved source and use **Generate key** under forwarding. The private key is sealed with `SESSION_SECRET` (like the Analyzer Observer key) and never shown; only its public key is. Without `SESSION_SECRET` set, the key cannot be stored.
+
+In own-identity mode, observers' `/status` heartbeats are not relayed: one observer going offline would mark the whole MeshMonitor identity offline. The target publishes MeshMonitor's own online status instead, with an offline last will.
+
+Forwarding never loops: forward clients only publish (they never subscribe), MeshMonitor's own key cannot log in to its own broker, a target cannot point at the broker's own port, and a frame MeshMonitor forwarded in the last two minutes is dropped if it comes back in.
+
+Forwarding carries only frames that passed the broker's limits, so it is capped by them too. A target that rejects the login five times in a row stops reconnecting until you save or reconnect the source.
+
+## Security notes
+
+- Upstream passwords and the static password are stored in the source config and returned to admins only; editors see them masked, viewers never see them. Changing a target's URL as an editor drops its stored password.

title: fix(automation): MeshCore telemetry triggers carry node name, key and role (#6397)
body:
Fixes #6397

## Problem
#6238 routed MeshCore remote telemetry into `trigger.telemetry`, but readings arrived keyed only by `nodeNumFromPubkey(publicKey)`, a hash of the key. In the trigger context:
- `{{ trigger.name }}` / `{{ trigger.publicKey }}` / `{{ trigger.roleName }}` did not exist.
- `{{ node.* }}` hydrates from the Meshtastic `nodes` table, which has no row for the hashed number.

A low-voltage alert therefore rendered only `{{ trigger.value }}` and couldn't name the node.

## Fix
- `MeshCoreRemoteTelemetryScheduler.requestTelemetryForNode` sends the contact's `publicKey`, `name` and `advType` with each emitted reading as `TelemetryEventMeta`. The scheduler tick already has the full `DbMeshCoreNode`, and the manual poll route already loads it, so this adds no extra DB reads.
- The event router passes these to `onTelemetry`. `buildTelemetryContext` adds `trigger.publicKey`, `trigger.name` and `trigger.roleName`, the same tokens the other MeshCore triggers (nodeDiscovered/nodeUpdated) already carry.
- MeshCore readings now use the MeshCore self-origin guard (`isSelfMeshCore`) instead of the Meshtastic one.
- `subjectNodeNum` stays the hashed number on purpose, so the persisted per-node telemetry cooldown (`automation_fire_state`) keeps its key across the upgrade and doesn't re-arm.
- The Substitutions help lists the three new tokens.

`{{ node.longName }}` still renders empty for MeshCore. This matches every other MeshCore trigger, which uses `trigger.name` for the name.

## Mesh impact checklist
1. **Airtime:** none. No new packets are sent. This only adds fields to an event that already fires.
2. **Spam:** no new fire paths. The existing once-per-node-per-hour telemetry floor is unchanged.
3. **Timers:** the cooldown key is unchanged, so neither a save nor an upgrade resets it.

## Tests
- `telemetryTrigger.test.ts`: a MeshCore reading goes through the real emitter batch, router and engine and renders `name|publicKey|Repeater|value`. A reading from our own MeshCore key is dropped.
- `meshcoreRoutes.test.ts`: the poll route now passes `name` to the scheduler.
- Automation, scheduler and MeshCore route suites pass. `tsc` is clean and `lint:ci` passes.
- Full local suite: everything passes except `linkPreviewRoutes.test.ts`. It fails the same way on unmodified `main` in this sandbox, which has no outbound DNS. The other early failures came from the uninitialised `protobufs/` submodule and pass once it is initialised.

Not included: the `get owner.info` side request from the issue. It would add a CLI round-trip (airtime) per poll, so it needs its own decision.

title: feat(mqtt): send Meshtastic messages over MQTT with no radio (#4305); fix PKI nonce layout
body:
Closes #4305.

Lets an MQTT bridge or broker source send Meshtastic messages with no radio attached, per the seven decisions in the issue. Off by default, per source.

## What changes
1. **Identity.** Each source gets its own generated node: an X25519 keypair, with the node number from `crc32(pubkey)` (the same derivation as firmware 2.8). Created once and never replaced. The private key is sealed with the SESSION_SECRET envelope, so the feature needs SESSION_SECRET set. Table `mqtt_native_identities` (migration 236) is per-source, in `BACKUP_TABLES` + `BACKUP_SECRET_TABLES`, and purged on source delete.
2. **Packet types (v1).** Channel text on Channel Database channels we hold a PSK for (AES-CTR, or AES-CCM on AEAD channels), PKI DMs (only when we hold a trusted key for the recipient), and NodeInfo. Nothing else: no traceroutes, key exchanges, or telemetry/position requests.
3. **Rate limit.** Sliding window, hard cap 6/min and 60/hour per source; admins can only lower it. Send timestamps are written to the DB *before* the publish, so a restart can't open a fresh window. NodeInfo doesn't count toward the cap.
4. **Hop limit 3** (clamped 0–7). **No automations:** the service needs a positive user id, its only callers are the send route and the NodeInfo scheduler (a guard test enforces this), and MQTT managers still have no `sendTextMessage`.
5. **NodeInfo** once on enable, then every 3 h, driven by a persisted `lastNodeInfoAt`. Only a real send writes it. The first tick runs a minute after start, so a restart is not a trigger, and a save sends only if one is due. Toggling off and on within 3 h does not re-announce. A failed publish backs off 10 min.
6. **Enable.** Per-source `mqttNativeSendEnabled`, off by default, with the downlink warning next to the toggle. Refused for subscribe-only bridges, when no root topic is known, or without SESSION_SECRET. The settings keys are deliberately *not* in `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS`, so the generic settings POST can't raise the caps or turn the feature on.
7. **Permission.** Send needs `messages:write` (`sourceIdFrom: 'params.id'`). A channel send by a non-admin also needs `canRead` on that channel. Changing the config needs `sources:write`.

**Wire format:** published to `{root}/2/e/{channel}/{ourNodeId}` (PKI DMs: `{root}/2/e/PKI/{ourNodeId}`), not retained. `gateway_id` is our node, `want_ack` is off, `ok_to_mqtt` is set, and `via_mqtt` is left for the gateway. Checked against firmware `develop` (`MQTT.cpp`, `CryptoEngine.cpp`) and against our own MQTT ingest/decrypt path in tests.

**Feedback loop:** our node num joins `getOwnNodeNums()`, so the #3914 self-origin guard skips our traffic on every source. Our own echo is dropped before ingest, and the row id format dedupes sends across restarts.

## Bug fix in shipped code: PKI nonce layout
`buildPkiNonce` (`pkiDecryptionService.ts`) built `[id][0][from][extraNonce low byte]`. Firmware `CryptoEngine::initNonce` builds `[id LE32][extraNonce LE32][from LE32][0]`.

title: feat(notifications): mesh-wide defaults, per-source overrides, cross-source dedup (#5729)
body:
Closes #5729.

Unifies notification settings across sources, per the seven decisions in the issue.

## What changes
1. **Dedup window** stays fixed at 60 s.
2. **Apprise and desktop hold an event 5 s**, then send once with every source that saw it. The deadline is fixed from the first copy; later copies only add their source. A clean shutdown flushes pending holds (2 s cap). Web Push is unchanged: it sends at once and updates silently.
3. **Web Push click** opens the first source that saw the event.
4. **Inactive and low-battery alerts dedup by node** (nodeNum for Meshtastic, key prefix for MeshCore). Inactive fires only when no readable source of the same protocol heard the node within the threshold.
5. **New-node alert per user**: a user who can read a source that already knew the node gets no alert. Meshtastic only; MeshCore still relies on the 60 s dedup.
6. **Mesh-wide default plus per-source overrides**: a `__mesh__` row in `user_notification_preferences`. Lookup order: source row → mesh default → pre-4.0 blob → built-in defaults. The default never grants permission; every delivery path still checks read access to the source.
7. **One Web Push subscription per browser**, filtered per source by permission, effective preferences, and the user's `pushSourceIds` list.

New routes: `GET/POST /push/preferences/mesh`, `DELETE /push/preferences/override` (`sourceIdFrom: 'query'`).

## Migration 235
- Adds `push_source_ids` and `mesh_defaults_saved` to `user_notification_preferences`.
- Collapses push subscriptions to one row per (user, endpoint), keeping the newest.
- Each user's subscribed sources become their `pushSourceIds` list, on a mesh row with every opt-in off and `meshDefaultsSaved` false.
- Per-source preference rows are untouched, so effective settings don't change until a user edits.
- Idempotent; tested on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL.

## Mesh impact
- **Airtime:** none. Sends no packets.
- **Spam:** fewer notifications. Cross-source duplicates collapse into one message.
- **Timers:** the 5 s hold reads no settings, and a second copy joins the existing hold rather than starting a new timer, so a save can't re-arm it. Inactive and low-battery cooldowns stay in memory as before; only their key changed.

## Known limits
- No-user push rows and the anonymous account get every source the anonymous account can read after the upgrade. Signed-in users keep exactly their old sources.
- A crash can drop up to 5 s of held Apprise/desktop messages. It can never cause a double send.
- Per-source switches are still ignored for inactive and low-battery alerts (existing #4020 rule).
- The mesh-wide panel covers the shared switches, Apprise URLs and the push source list. Keywords, templates and thresholds can be set mesh-wide through the API only.

## Tests
54 related files, 977 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. PG/MySQL suites ran. `tsc` and `lint:ci` are clean.

title: feat(privacy): hide no-MQTT-consent nodes from anonymous viewers (#5156)
body:
Part of #5156 (the `ok_to_mqtt` half). Public-instance mode stays open for a later PR.

## What it does
New per-source setting **Anonymous viewers → hide nodes that declined MQTT** (`anonHideMqttNoConsent`), **off by default**. When on, signed-out viewers (and embeds) no longer see a node, or any of its data, if:
- the last `ok_to_mqtt` bit we decoded for it from an MQTT-delivered packet is **false**, and
- it has never been heard directly over RF on that source.

Unknown consent (no bitfield, undecryptable, pre-bitfield firmware) shows. Signed-in users are never filtered. An RF hearing keeps the node visible for the life of its row (maintainer's call).

## Data
Migration 234 adds three nullable per-source columns on `nodes`: `mqttOkToMqtt`, `mqttOkToMqttAt`, `rfDirectLastHeard`. No backfill, so every existing node starts as unknown/visible.

Captured in `mqttConsentCapture.ts` (reuses `readBitfieldOkToMqtt` + `classifyNodeTransport`) from `processMeshPacket` and MQTT `ingestServiceEnvelope`:
- MQTT-delivered (mechanism MQTT, `via_mqtt`, or MQTT path) with a readable bitfield → consent stamp. LORA + `via_mqtt` (downlink rebroadcast) counts as MQTT.
- RF with `via_mqtt` clear, not a replay (S&F, virtual node, NodeDB replay) → `rfDirectLastHeard`.

## Filtering
One helper, `mqttConsentVisibility.ts`, wired into the shared visibility paths (`loadNodeViewAccess`/`canViewNode`, `buildPositionFilter`, `checkNodeChannelAccess`, `resolveNodePositionScope`, channel-permission masks) plus explicit filters on messages, traceroutes (dropped whole if the node is either end or any hop), neighbor info, packet monitor, MQTT packet log, unified views and embeds. Follow-up commits close the remaining anonymous endpoints that can name a node: packet distribution / node-activity / relay-nodes (exclusion inside the SQL), route-segment longest-active / record-holder (best *visible* row), direct-neighbors, ATAK contacts, mesh issues, assets, `/nodes/:nodeNum/sources`, copy-candidates, identity changes/merges, auto-favorite status, position estimate, survey neighbours, solar, mqtt-violations, heard-by.

**Fails closed:** if the hidden set can't load, anonymous viewers see none of the affected nodes (every source if settings/sources can't be read; that source if its node read fails). Logged as a warning.

Socket.io (no anonymous sessions) and the v1 API (token required) are not anonymous.

## Known limits
- Pure counts still include hidden nodes: packet `/stats` totals, unread counts, search totals, survey node/hop totals.
- Some lists filter after paging (messages, MQTT packet log, mqtt-violations, mesh issues), so a page can come back short and some `total` fields are unfiltered.
- Where rows merge several sources with no per-row source, a node hidden on any of them is hidden.
- Mesh-issue `evidence` is not scrubbed of other node numbers.
- Not part of this PR: a cross-source bug in `getLatestNeighborInfoPerNode` (separate PR).

## Mesh impact checklist
1. Airtime: non

body:
Closes #6181. Closes #6321.

Both track firmware changes on `develop` that are not in a tagged release yet. Minimal scope, per maintainer.

## #6181: LoRa transparent mode — detect and warn
With `LoRaConfig.transparent_mode` on, the node hands every LoRa frame to the client still encrypted and does no decoding, relaying, ACKs or MQTT. MeshMonitor would show no decoded traffic and sends would fail.
