- **LoRa config page:** read-only checkbox with the same warning. MeshMonitor cannot turn it on.
- **Bug fix:** `createSetLoRaConfigMessage` dropped the field, and `set_config` replaces the whole LoRaConfig, so any LoRa save from MeshMonitor would silently turn transparent mode off. The field now rides along, always taken from what the device last reported (Config tab, import, restore, Admin Commands local/remote). The request body is never trusted for it.

## #6321: protobufs bump + bootloader version
- `protobufs` submodule b7fde64 → 0adaccd (upstream master, 4 commits). Additive only: `DeviceMetadata.bootloader_version`, `FieldMetadata.sensitive` tags on secret fields, a new `ClientNotification.Type` value (not read in `src/`), ATAK voice-profile messages. - Info tab shows **Bootloader Version** (`major.minor.patch`) for the local node when non-zero (nRF52 only), via `/api/config` and `/api/poll`, same path as BLE address (#6157).
- `sensitive`-driven redaction is left for later.

## Mesh impact checklist
1. Airtime: none. Read/display only, no new sends.
2. Spam: none. No events or notifications.
3. Timers: none touched.

## Tests
New: `LoRaConfigSection.transparentMode`, `protobufService.transparentMode`, `adminRoutes.transparentMode` (route harness), `bootloaderVersion`. title: fix(meshtastic): send position requests with an empty Position (#6047)
body:
Fixes #6047.

## Problem
Exchange Position from one source went unanswered for every MQTT-reached target, while traceroute from the same source worked and Exchange Position from a second source worked. The issue thread narrowed it to the request contents:
- Working source sent a 5-byte request (empty Position).
- Failing source sent a 21-byte request carrying its own lat/lon (its node has a fixed position, so `sendPositionRequest` attached it).
- With position sharing turned off on the failing radio's channel 0 (so the request went out empty), the exchange was answered at once.

Likely mechanism: a relay running Traffic Management position dedup drops a position-bearing packet as a duplicate with no NAK; an empty Position has no lat/lon and is never deduped. Not confirmed on a device in the path; the test confirms the coordinates are what matter.

## Fix
- `createPositionRequestMessage` always encodes an empty `Position` with `wantResponse`; the `position` parameter is gone.
- `sendPositionRequest` no longer looks up the local node's position or position config.
- Applies to every caller: Exchange Position button, v1 actions API, automation engine, aircraft position requests.

Trade-off (decided by the maintainer): the far node no longer learns our position from an exchange. It still gets it from our normal position broadcasts. The reply never depended on the request's contents.

## Mesh impact checklist
1. Airtime: lower. Same number of packets, payload shrinks from ~21 to 0 bytes.
2. Spam: none. No new sends, events or notifications.
3. Timers: none touched.

## Tests
- New `meshtasticProtobufService.positionRequest.test.ts`: payload is empty, `wantResponse` set, portnum POSITION_APP.
- Hop-limit test updated for the new signature.
- 19 related suites pass (341 tests): protobuf service, manager tx guards, mesh request routes, v1 actions, automation deps/pins, aircraft position requests. `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` and `lint:ci` clean.

title: fix(meshcore): decode Cayenne-LPP telemetry locally so altitude no longer truncates sensors
body:
Fixes #6389

## Problem
MeshMonitor decoded MeshCore remote telemetry with the pinned meshcore.js (`Yeraze/meshcore.js@bd710fcc`) `CayenneLpp.parse()`. That parser handles only about a dozen types, and its `default:` branch returns early. Cayenne-LPP records carry no length byte, so when the parser doesn't know a type it can't find where the next record starts. A repeater with a BME280/BMP280 sends altitude (type 121) right after pressure, so every record after the altitude was dropped. In the report, that meant the INA3221 voltage, current and power channels.

## Fix
- New `src/server/utils/meshcoreCayenneLpp.ts`: a local decoder that knows every fixed-size type in the firmware's ElectronicCats `CayenneLPP.h` (sizes and multipliers taken from that header). It covers analog in/out, frequency, altitude, distance, energy, direction, unixtime, accelerometer, gyrometer, colour, switch and digital I/O. It stops only at `00 00` padding, an unknown or variable-length type (polyline), or a record cut short by the end of the buffer. Records decoded before the stop are kept.
- For types meshcore.js already decoded, the scaling is unchanged (voltage, current and luminosity are still read as signed), so stored history keeps its meaning.
- `meshcoreNativeBackend.ts` `request_telemetry` now calls `parseCayenneLpp(responseData)` instead of `mod.CayenneLpp.parse()`. The `raw` payload relayed to the Virtual Node is unchanged.
- `meshcoreRemoteTelemetryScheduler` already maps 121, 118, 130, 2 and others in `LPP_TYPE_NAMES`, so the new records show up as `mc_altitude_chN` and so on with no further change.

This removes the need for a fork bump (meshcore-dev/meshcore.js#46) to fix this issue. The fork can still be updated separately.

## Mesh impact checklist
1. Airtime: none. No new packets; this only changes how a reply we already receive is decoded.
2. Spam: none. More telemetry rows per existing poll, and no new events or notifications.
3. Timers: none touched.

## Tests
- `src/server/utils/meshcoreCayenneLpp.test.ts`: decodes the BME280 + INA3221 sequence from the report past the altitude record. Also covers signed altitude and analog values, unsigned 32-bit distance, frequency, energy, GPS and three-axis objects, and stopping on padding, unknown types and truncated records.
- The MeshCore backend and telemetry-scheduler suites pass locally (266 tests). `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` and `lint:ci` are clean.
- `meshcoreNativeBackend.test.ts` fails to collect locally because the `re2` native module isn't built in this sandbox (`npm ci --ignore-scripts`). The same failure happens without this change, and CI installs fresh.

-- Authored by Roger 🤓

title: feat: Direct RF Contacts history for Meshtastic and MeshCore (#6210)
body:
Closes #6210.

Adds a long-lived history of nodes each source hears **directly over RF** (0 hops), for both Meshtastic and MeshCore, with a report, a node-detail section, and a fixed Network survey table.

## What changed
- **Storage:** new `direct_rf_contacts` daily rollup (migration 233), one row per source + node + UTC day: first/last heard direct, reception count, best SNR/RSSI, SNR/RSSI sums for averages. Per-source, scoped with `withSourceScope`, in `BACKUP_TABLES`, cleared on node purge / source delete.
- **Retention:** `direct_rf_contacts_retention_days`, default **30**, clamped 1–365, hourly sweep (skipped on a restore boot). Input sits beside Coverage retention in Settings.
- **Meshtastic rule:** not our own node; not S&F / virtual-node replay; `viaMqtt !== true` and transport not MQTT (catches MQTT-downlink rebroadcasts over LoRa, per the issue comment); RF transport; `hopStart` present and hops away = 0; `isLiveReception` and not a NodeDB replay (#5426). All portnums count. MQTT ingest never feeds it.
- **MeshCore rule:** companion `ota_packet` (LogRxData 0x88) ADVERTs at zero hops, Ed25519-verified, own replay guard, keyed by the 32-byte public key.
- **Writes:** buffered per (source, node, day), flushed every 5 s (or at 500 keys); one-shot timer, flushed on shutdown.
- **API:** `GET /api/sources/:id/direct-rf-contacts?from=&to=` and `…/node/:nodeKey`, `requirePermission('nodes','read',{ sourceIdFrom })`, distance only when both positions pass the position filters.
- **UI:**
  - Direct RF Contacts report (Analysis tab, next to Coverage Report): source picker, 24h/7d/30d/custom, sortable, CSV export.
  - "Direct RF" section on Meshtastic and MeshCore node detail: last/first heard direct, 30-day count, best SNR, per-day bars.
  - Info tab Network survey "Heard directly" now reads the rollup, adds First/Last heard columns, and no longer empties when packet_log rolls over.

## Known limits
- Counts are per UTC day, so a window edge that cuts a day counts the whole day (first/last times are exact). "Median" from the issue is shown as average.
- MeshCore: only adverts can key a row (other payloads carry a colliding 1-byte hash). Repeater/serial MeshCore sources emit no `ota_packet`, so only companions feed it. A `shareContactZeroHop` re-send reads as direct (same gap as Coverage Report).
- No backfill; history starts at deploy.

title: feat(security): opt-in node-name anti-spam sanitizer (#6382)
body:
Closes #6382

## What

An opt-in filter that removes invite links from node names before MeshMonitor stores them. An admin turns it on in **Global Settings → Security → Node name anti-spam**. It is off by default.

`NodeName t.me/spam_channel` → `NodeName [spammer]`

## Design

**Pure sanitizer** (`src/utils/nodeNameSanitizer.ts`)
- Built-in rules: any `http(s)://` link, plus `t.me/`, `telegram.me/`, `telegram.dog/`, `discord.gg/`, `wa.me/`, `chat.whatsapp.com/` (host + `/` + handle).
- Matching runs on a normalised copy: NFKC folding (full-width letters), zero-width characters dropped, spaced or bracketed dots allowed (`t . me`, `t[.]me`, `t(dot)me`, `t。me`). Each normalised character maps back to its original span, so only the matched text is replaced and the rest of the name keeps its spelling.
- Only the link is replaced. Adjacent links share one placeholder. Leftover whitespace collapses. A name that was only a link becomes the placeholder.
- Byte limit: a Meshtastic long name stays within 24 bytes (fw 2.8), or the original size up to 39 for older firmware; short name 4; MeshCore 31. When too long, the kept text is trimmed by whole code points. The placeholder is never cut.
- Admin patterns, one per line: a plain host (`spam.example`) gets the built-in host treatment; anything else compiles through `compileUserRegex` (RE2, case-insensitive). Max 256 characters, max 50 patterns; a pattern that matches the empty string is rejected. Invalid patterns are a 400 at save; an invalid stored row is skipped at load rather than turning the filter off.

**Seams** (one per protocol, in the repository layer)
- Meshtastic: `NodesRepository.upsertNode` (`src/db/repositories/nodes.ts`). `DatabaseService.upsertNodeAsync` calls it, but `mqttIngestion.ts` stub/refresh paths call `databaseService.nodes.upsertNode` directly, so the repo method is the only seam every path shares.
- MeshCore: `MeshCoreRepository.upsertNode` (`src/db/repositories/meshcore.ts`), right after the existing printable-name cleanup.
- Rules are cached in a module slot (`src/utils/nodeNameSanitizerRuntime.ts`, same pattern as `positionIngestConfig.ts`), loaded before `bootstrapSources` and reloaded after a settings save or reset. No settings read per packet.

**Own node is never rewritten.** A resolver (installed at startup) asks the source's manager: Meshtastic `getLocalNodeInfo().nodeNum`, MeshCore `getLocalNode().publicKey`. MeshCore rows flagged `isLocalNode` are also skipped. The re-scan also checks the saved `localNodeNum[_<sourceId>]` setting for a source whose manager is offline. The check is per source: a source's own node heard as a remote node on another source is cleaned there.

**Settings**: `nodeNameSanitizeEnabled`, `nodeNameSanitizeBuiltins`, `nodeNameSanitizeCustomPatterns` (JSON array), `nodeNameSanitizePlaceholder` (default `[spammer]`, max 24 bytes). In `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS`, `GLOBAL_ONLY_SETTINGS_KEYS` and `ADMIN_ONLY_SETTINGS_KEYS`. The Security card's other items (`Pk

title: fix: grant remote_admin from Users tab; BASE_URL trailing slashes
body:
Fixes four bugs found while writing real tests in #6380.

## 1. `remote_admin` could not be granted from the Users tab
`remote_admin` is a per-source resource (MeshCore remote admin routes check `remote_admin:read` for session/status and `:write` for login/CLI), but it was missing from `PERMISSION_KEYS`, so it never showed in the grid and was never sent on save. Added it with label `users.remote_admin_permission` and a tooltip. The server PUT has no allowlist and scopes it via `SOURCEY_RESOURCES`, so no server change. A server-vs-UI resource diff found no other missing resource.

Note: the row shows for every source type, though the routes exist only for MeshCore; a grant on other sources is inert.

## 2. `channel_database` got `viewOnMap: false` on save
`startsWith('channel_')` matched it. Now `/^channel_\d+$/` (`isChannelSlot`), also used at the grid render sites for consistency.

## 3. BASE_URL stripped only one trailing slash
`//` → `/`, `/foo//` → `/foo/`. Now strips all: `replace(/\/+$/, '')`.

## 4. Dead `segment === '..'` branch removed
Unreachable: leading-slash normalisation runs first, so any `..` segment means the string contains `/..`, which the earlier check rejects. Tests pin `..`, `/mesh/..` and `/mesh/..//` as rejected.

## Tests
- `UsersTab.permissionSave.test.tsx`: remote_admin row present and sent on save, scoped to the source; channel_database saved without viewOnMap, channel_1 keeps it.
- `environment.baseUrl.test.ts`: multiple trailing slashes; traversal cases.
- Locally: 6 related files, 55 tests pass. tsc and lint via CI.

title: test: real coverage for gaps left by #6379
body:
#6379 removed tests that ran copies of production logic written inside the test file. This PR adds tests that import and run the real code for each gap it left. For each gap I broke the production code on purpose, confirmed the new tests failed, then reverted.

## 1. BASE_URL validation (`loadEnvironmentConfig()`)
- **File:** `src/server/config/environment.baseUrl.test.ts` (17 tests, new)
- **What it tests:** sets `process.env.BASE_URL` and calls the real `loadEnvironmentConfig()`. Covers unset, empty and `/`; leading-slash fix; trailing-slash removal; multi-segment paths; traversal rejection (`../`, `/..`, `..\`, bare `..`) that falls back to `''` with `baseUrlProvided: false` and logs an error; no false positive on `/v1..2`; the warning for special characters.
- **Mutation check:** removing the trailing-slash `slice` failed 3 tests. Disabling the `includes('../' | '..\\' | '/..')` check failed the `..\` case. Disabling the later `segment === '..'` check failed nothing, because the earlier `includes('/..')` check catches every such input once the leading slash is added. That later check is dead code (see Findings).

## 2. Channel-database response shape (`transformChannelForResponse`)
- **File:** `src/server/routes/channelDatabaseRoutes.responseShape.test.ts` (12 tests, new). Uses `createRouteTestApp()` with real session, auth and `checkPermissionAsync`. Only the repository data reads are stubbed.
- **What it tests:** admin and non-admin `channel_database:write` callers get the raw PSK. Read-only and anonymous callers with a per-entry grant get no `psk` key and a `(hidden)` preview, on both the list and by-id routes, with no key-prefix bytes anywhere in the body. Empty, null or missing PSKs show `(none)`. Two different PSKs give the same masked preview, so the preview can't be used to match channels. The test also covers field passthrough, the defaults for `enforceNameValidation`, `useAead` and `sortOrder`, and protocol normalisation (`meshcore` stays `meshcore`, any other value becomes `meshtastic`).
- **No production change.** The function was already exported, but it is tested through the routes.
- **Mutation check:** leaking the old 8-character preview plus the raw `psk` to read-only callers failed 5 tests. Dropping the `useAead` default and protocol normalisation failed 2.

## 3. Token insert
- **Production change (small extraction):** the three automation editors (`AutoAnnounceSection`, `AutoWelcomeSection`, `MeshCoreAutoAnnounceSection`) each had their own copy of the splice logic. That logic now lives in one pure helper, `insertTokenAtSelection(text, token, selection | null)` in `src/utils/tokenInsert.ts`. Each component still handles its own focus and caret restore. Behaviour is unchanged.
- **Files:** `src/utils/tokenInsert.test.ts` (11 tests: caret, selection replace, select-all, append fallback when no textarea, UTF-16 caret) and one wiring test added to `src/components/AutoAnnounceSection.test.tsx`. That test renders the component,

title: ci: shard the test suite 3 ways per Node version
body:
## Summary
- The `test` job now runs as 3 shards per Node version (`vitest run --shard=k/3`), 9 jobs total, `fail-fast: false`.
- New `test-summary` job, named `Test Suite (<node>)`, keeps the check names the `protect main` ruleset and the Dependabot auto-merge regexp require. It passes only when every shard passed.

## Why
The #6376 timing probe showed test bodies are only ~22% of the test step; the rest is per-file fork + module import across ~2,650 files. That overhead splits almost evenly across runners, so 3 shards should take the test step from ~20–25 min to roughly 8–10 min. More workers on one runner would not help: 4 already saturate it.

## Cost
9 test runners per CI run instead of 3, each also starting PG and MySQL service containers.

title: perf(tests): faster CI test run — template test DB, lean setup, lazy fallbackManager, quiet logs, static-check job
body:
CI "Run tests" takes 21-30 min per Node leg. Vitest's own breakdown is import 46%, tests 31%, environment 10%, setup 8%. This PR cuts the fixed costs behind those numbers without touching what the tests check.

**No tests deleted.** No test was merged or skipped either. Six test files changed, all because of change 3 (below).

## 1. Template test DB (`src/server/test-helpers/testDb.ts`)

**What:** `createTestDb()` used to run all ~230 SQLite migrations on every call (150-200 ms), and ~160 suites call it in `beforeEach`, about 2,100 calls per run. Now each test file builds the migrated DB once, serializes it, and opens each call's DB from that buffer with `new Database(buffer)`, which takes about 1 ms. The function's signature and return shape are unchanged, and it takes no options. Each call still gets an independent in-memory DB. Connection-level pragmas that migrations touch (`foreign_keys`, `legacy_alter_table`) are not stored in the image, so they are read from the build connection and set again on each copy.

**Not changed:** `DatabaseService`'s constructor. Its migration loop is production code, and adding a test-only shortcut there is neither simple nor safe.

**Measured (local, `--maxWorkers=2`):** `automationEngineService.test.ts` + `telemetry.extra.test.ts` + `auth.test.ts` took **23.4 s before and 2.8 s after**, with the same 223 passed and 92 skipped.

## 2. Lean `src/test/setup.ts`

**What:** `@testing-library/react`, the jest-dom matchers and `vectorSupport` (which pulls in React) now load through a top-level `await import()` behind `typeof window !== 'undefined'`. Only jsdom files pay for them. `expect.extend(matchers)`, the vectorSupport `beforeEach` and RTL `cleanup` still register before any test in a jsdom file runs. The `react-i18next` and `emoji-picker-react` mocks, the `localStorage` / `matchMedia` stubs and the `waitForBackgroundTasks` `afterAll` are unchanged. The three node-env files that mention BaseMap or jest-dom only scan source text.

**Why:** about 1,900 node-environment files paid ~130 ms each for DOM tooling they never used.

**Measured:** five node-env files went from "setup 16%" to "setup 2%" of the run (1.25 s → 1.13 s wall).

## 3. Lazy `fallbackManager` (`src/server/fallbackManagerHolder.ts`)

**What:** `resolveSourceManager.ts` and `localNodeNameForSource.ts` no longer import `meshtasticManager.ts`. `meshtasticManager.ts` registers `fallbackManager` with a new holder module right after creating it, and the helpers call `getFallbackManager()` at call time. The call sites stay synchronous. The holder imports nothing at runtime.

**Why:** the static import pulled the 17k-line manager into ~400 test files; the audit estimates ~106 without it. It also closes the import cycle documented in `meshtasticManager.ts` (meshtasticManager → distanceDeleteScheduler → autoDeleteByDistanceService → resolveSourceManager → meshtasticManager).

**Production:** behaviour is unchanged. `server.ts` imports `meshtasticManager.ts` s

title: feat(meshcore): import/export MeshCore One contact-share tokens (#6370)
body:
## Summary

MeshMonitor can now read and write the contact-share token that MeshCore One uses: `<PUBKEYHEX:type:name>`. A token in a message gets an import button. The MeshCore channel and DM composers get a **+** menu with **Share contact** and **Share my contact info**.

I wrote this from the token description in the issue. No MeshCore One code was copied.

## Import

- Tokens are found in MeshCore channel messages, DMs and room posts on every MeshCore source type. The token text stays as sent, with an import button next to it. The button uses `UiIcon` `identity` (lucide `IdCard`), which was already in the registry, so no emoji and no new registry entry.
- Clicking the button opens a modal built on the shared `Modal`. It shows the name, type and public key, with **Import** and **Cancel**.
  - Import is enabled only on a connected Companion source when the user has `nodes:write`. Otherwise the modal says why (shared hook `useContactTokenImport`).
  - A full radio contact list is confirmed inside the modal ("Import anyway"), not with `window.confirm`.
  - The modal shows when a contact is already on the radio, and refuses the source's own key.
- The Nodes view **Import** dialog (`MeshCoreNodesView` `handleImport`) tries the token first, then falls back to the signed-advert hex or `meshcore://` input. It has the same in-place confirm for a full list.
- Backend: new `POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/contacts/import-token`, body `{ token, confirmFull? }`.
  - Same chain as add-to-device: `meshcoreDeviceLimiter`, `requireAuth()`, `requirePermission('nodes', 'write', { sourceIdFrom: 'params.id' })`. Uses `ok()`/`fail()` and writes an audit event.
  - The server parses the token again with the shared module.
  - `MeshCoreManager.importContactFromToken` calls `addContactToDevice` with a new optional `seed: { advType, name }`. That reuses the has-contact check, full-table confirm, favourite protection and table-full handling as they are. The write is `CMD_ADD_UPDATE_CONTACT` with a flood (unknown) out-path.
  - The add-to-device outcome switch moved into a shared `sendAddContactResult()` so both routes answer the same way.
- Decisions:
  - **A contact already on the radio is left alone.** `add_contact` skips it, so its out-path, flags and name are not changed.
  - **Stored data beats the unsigned token.** An existing node keeps its name and type. A `meshcore_nodes` row is written for the source only when it is missing, or to fill a missing name or type.
  - **The source's own key is refused** (`400 CANNOT_IMPORT_SELF`).
  - **Import lifts a removal tombstone** (#3878), so the contact refresh after the add keeps a contact the user removed earlier.

## Export

- `MessageComposeInput` (the composer shared by Meshtastic and MeshCore) takes a new optional `insertMenuItems` prop. When it is set, a **+** button sits between the text box and Send.
  - The menu (`ComposeInsertMenu`) is protocol-neutral and data-driven, so new entries need no change to the composer.

title: fix(messages): release queued channel sends on the local radio ACK (#6373)
body:
Fixes #6373

## Problem
A channel broadcast never gets a target-node ACK, because its `toNodeId` is `!ffffffff`. In `processRoutingErrorMessage`, the own-radio ACK branch marked the row `delivered` and returned without calling `messageQueue.handleAck(requestId)`. Every queued channel send (timer triggers, auto-ack, auto-responder, geofences, auto-welcome, the v1 API) therefore stayed in `pendingAcks` until the 5-minute orphan sweep (`cleanupOrphanedAcks`) failed it. The visible results were:

- a false `❌ ... message failed to channel N: ACK timeout` warning,
- a `timeout` event in `message_events` after the real `delivered` event,
- the queue's `onFailure` firing instead of `onSuccess`.

## Fix
In the own-radio ACK branch, a non-DM message now calls `messageQueue.handleAck(requestId)`, because for a broadcast the local transmit ACK is final. A DM still waits for the target's ACK, so DM retries work as before. The release also runs when the row was already `delivered`.

## Mesh impact checklist
1. **Airtime:** none. No packets are added or removed. Channel sends already use `maxAttempts = 1`, so nothing was being resent.
2. **Spam / indirect paths:** the only change is that `onSuccess` fires instead of `onFailure` for channel sends. I checked every `enqueue` caller (meshtasticManager + `routes/v1/messages.ts`): their callbacks only log or mark rows, and none sends a packet.
3. **Safety timers:** none are touched.

## Tests
- Added 4 regression tests in `src/server/meshtasticManager.deliveryEvents.test.ts`:
  - a channel send is released on the local ACK;
  - it is released even when the row was already delivered;
  - a DM is *not* released on the local ACK;
  - a DM is released on the target ACK.
- The two channel tests fail without the fix and pass with it.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json`: clean. `lint:ci`: no in-repo FAILs.
- Full Vitest run: 36,898 passed, 6 failed, 1,993 skipped (PG/MySQL containers were not running). All 6 failures are in `src/server/routes/linkPreviewRoutes.test.ts`, and they fail the same way with this change reverted. They look like a sandbox network issue and are unrelated to this change; CI is the authority.

-- Authored by Roger 🤓

title: fix(backup): MySQL backup list 500 from a cross-table collation compare
body:
## Summary
`GET /api/backup/list` returned **500 on MySQL**. The hardware system test (API exercise, MySQL backend) caught it on the 4.17.3-rc6 bump PR (#6371). The bug shipped in rc5 with #6313.

**Cause:** the "unowned backup" predicate compared `backup_history.sourceId` to `SELECT id FROM sources` inside SQL. On MySQL the two columns can hold different collations: `backup_history` comes from the baseline (`utf8mb4_unicode_ci`), while `sources` (migration 020) takes the server default (`utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci`). The comparison fails with `ER_CANT_AGGREGATE_2COLLATIONS`.

**Fix:** read the live source ids first and compare against them as literals (`notInArray(col, ids)`). With no sources, every row counts as unowned.

**Test:** the MySQL fixture in `backupHistory.perSource.test.ts` now uses the production collations. The existing `listUnowned` test fails without the fix (`Illegal mix of collations`) and passes with it. Ran with PostgreSQL and MySQL containers up: 52/52 across 5 backup test files, 0 skipped. Server tsc clean, `lint:ci` 0 FAIL.

Mesh impact: none.

body:
Batch P6 of the 4.17.3 pre-release review: the seven items where the maintainer set the limit. Each is built as written in the tracker's "Decisions" table.

## M3: automatic MeshCore traces notify only on a new opt-in

**What was wrong:** every auto-pathfinding discovery and every scheduled trace sent a push, Apprise or desktop alert under `notifyOnTraceroute`. That comes to about one alert per contact per day for every subscriber.

**Fix:**
- New per-(user, source) preference `notifyOnAutoTrace`, default **off**. It is migration 232 on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL: idempotent `ADD COLUMN DEFAULT FALSE` through the shared helpers, registered with a `settingsKey`.
- `notificationService.notifyTraceroute(..., { automatic })` sends automatic results to the new key. User-started traces and discoveries keep `notifyOnTraceroute`.
- **Traces:** `origin` `schedule` and `automation` count as automatic. `manual`, `api` and an unset origin count as user-started. The Automation Engine's `traceroute` op now passes `origin: 'automation'`, which before was logged as `manual`.
- **Discoveries:** `discoverContactPath(key, { automatic })` keeps a short-lived entry per contact, with a TTL of the firmware timeout and at least 60 s. The push reply consumes it. Auto-pathfinding passes `automatic: true`. A reply nobody is waiting for, or one that arrives past its window, counts as automatic, which is the quiet side.
- **UI:** a toggle on the Notifications tab for MeshCore Companion only, via a new `autoTrace` capability. It shows help text that warns about the volume. Meshtastic behaviour is unchanged.

**Tests:**
- Origin mapping for traces.
- Discovery origin: user, automatic, unrequested, expired, consumed.
- `notifyTraceroute` preference key.
- Route save and validation.
- Per-source repository isolation.
- Capability table and toggle render.
- Migration idempotency on SQLite, plus a PostgreSQL and MySQL container test (`232_…pgmysql.test.ts`, both ran).

## M4: bounded split-message queue

**What was wrong:** `SplitSequenceLock` was an unbounded promise chain. A cooldown-0 responder could build a backlog of 3-part replies that went out hours late.

**Fix:** `SplitSequenceLock.run(fn, { key })`:
- It drops a new sequence when one with the same key is already **waiting**. One running plus one waiting per key is allowed.
- It drops any sequence that waited more than **2 minutes** before its turn.
- A drop returns `ok: false, dropped: 'duplicate' | 'stale'` and never throws. Nothing retries it. The Automation Engine's run log names the drop instead of "send rejected".
- A duplicate drop logs at info the first time per key, then at debug. A stale drop logs at info.

The key is the trigger plus the real destination (DM pubkey or nodeNum, or the channel list):
- **MeshCore:** `label` already carries the trigger id.
- **Meshtastic Auto Responder:** now passes `auto-responder:<triggerIdx>`, because its label was the same for every trigger.
- **Automation Engine:** has no a

title: fix(meshcore): 4.17.3 review P3 — MeshCore senders (Auto Welcome cap, MeshWars hops, split floor)
body:
Fixes batch P3 (MeshCore senders) from the 4.17.3 pre-release review.

## H1: Auto Welcome hourly cap did not hold against a burst

**What was wrong:** the cap was checked when a contact was found, but the send time was recorded only after the 30 s pre-send delay. A burst of new contacts inside one delay window (or a `refreshContacts` flushing many parked nameless keys) all passed the check, so N welcomes went out with no upper bound. `recordWelcomeSend` was also an unlocked read-modify-write, so close fires could drop each other's entries.

**Fix** (limits unchanged: DM default, 6/hr, drop-not-queue, 3 hops, 30 s delay):
- `withAutoWelcomeLock(sourceId, fn)`: a per-source promise chain in `meshcoreAutoWelcome.ts`. The decide-and-reserve step runs under it, and the manager counts a reserved slot for each welcome waiting out the delay (`decideAutoWelcome` takes `reservedSlots`). Anything over the cap is dropped, not queued.
- `fireAutoWelcome` re-runs the decision under the lock just before sending (enabled flag, already-welcomed, cap minus its own slot, and the contact as it is now). If it doesn't send, it releases the slot. The slot is released only after `recordWelcomeSend` persists, so the cap can overcount for a moment but never undercounts.
- `recordWelcomeSend` runs under the same lock.
- `cancelPendingAutoWelcomes()` clears pending timers and frees their slots. It runs on `disconnect()`, `teardownTransportOnly()` and the unexpected-link-loss path. A decision still in flight sees an epoch change and drops.
- `flushPendingNewNodeNotifications` (called from `refreshContacts`) returns early while `newNodeNotifySuppressed` is set. It already went through `notifyNewNodeDiscovered` → `checkAutoWelcome`, so it now gets the same reservation.

**Tests:** `meshcoreManager.autoWelcomeCap.test.ts` (real `:memory:` DB, fake timers, `sendMessage` stubbed):
- 10 contacts in one window: 6 scheduled, 6 sent, nothing queued afterwards
- disabling during the delay sends 0
- a key welcomed elsewhere during the delay is dropped
- disconnect cancels pending welcomes
- recorded sends count against the cap
- the flush stays quiet while suppression is on

`meshcoreAutoWelcome.test.ts` covers `reservedSlots` and 6 concurrent `recordWelcomeSend` calls keeping every entry. Mutation-checked: with the reservation or the record lock removed, these tests fail.

## L4: Auto Welcome greeted Repeaters / Room Servers / Sensors

**Fix:** `decideAutoWelcome` skips advType 2/3/4 (`not_chat_node`). The send-time re-check reads the live contact, so a type learned during the delay is honoured. **Choice to note:** an unknown type (0 or absent) is still greeted, since early adverts often lack it. The task says "Companion only"; flip this if unknown should be skipped too.

**Tests:** decision table (2/3/4 skipped; 1/0/absent greeted) and manager-level tests, including a type learned mid-delay.

## H2: MeshWars forwarder off-by-one on `hops`

**What was wrong:** `attributeChannelEcho`

body:
Fixes batch P1 Security from the 4.17.3 pre-release review (tracker `docs/internal/dev-notes/RELEASE_4173_REVIEW.md`).

## B1 (BLOCKER): v1 API returned every MeshCore channel PSK to `messages:write`
**Wrong:** `routes/v1/channels.ts` used one helper for visibility and key exposure, so the legacy `messages` fallback also handed out `psk`. Any token with `messages:write` read every slot's key, including slots above 7. The UI (`channelRoutes.ts`) needs admin or `channel_<id>:write`.
**Fix:** split the helper. `canReadMeshcoreSlot` keeps the `messages` fallback for visibility only. `canSeeMeshcorePsk` mirrors the UI: admin, or `channel_<id>:write` on this source for slots 0-7; above 7, admin only. Applied to both `GET /` and `GET /:channelId`.
**Test:** `v1/meshcore.read.test.ts` (harness): `messages:read+write` sees slots 0/1/12 with no `psk` (list and single); `channel_1:write` (plus `messages:write`) gets only slot 1's key; admin gets all three. The old case that asserted `psk` under `messages:write` encoded the bug and now asserts the reverse.

## M1: deleting a source left its MeshCore device key behind
**Wrong:** `secretPurges` in `DELETE /api/sources/:id` missed `meshcore_source_pki_keys` (#6195).
**Fix:** added `meshcoreSourcePkiKeys.deleteBySourceId`. I also checked every per-source table in `BACKUP_SECRET_TABLES`. A test showed that `channels` rows (PSKs in the clear) also survived a source delete, so the purge now drops the source's channel slots too, using only the existing `getAllChannels` and `deleteChannel` repository methods.
**Test:** `sourceRoutes.deleteCleanup.test.ts`: source A's device key and channel slots go; source B's stay; a node purge on a live source keeps the device key.

## M2: gateway membership bypassed `packetmonitor:read` and channel `viewOnMap`
**Wrong:** `buildSourceDashboard` returned every MQTT `fromNode` and gateway to anyone with `nodes:read`.
**Fix:** membership now needs `packetmonitor:read` on the source as well, and its rows are cut to `fromNode`s already in the payload's filtered `nodes`.
**Test:** `sourceDashboardData.gatewayMembership.test.ts`: `nodes:read` alone gets no membership. With both grants the viewer sees both nodes' rows. A node on a channel without `viewOnMap` has its rows dropped. Existing cases now seed node rows.

## L15: security clear and digest checked the grant on any source
**Wrong:** `POST /security/nodes/:nodeNum/clear` and `POST /security/digest/send` acted on `body.sourceId` but did not check permission on that source.
**Fix:** both now take `{ sourceIdFrom: 'body', requireSourceId: true }`. Adding that alone changes nothing: `security` is a global resource (not in `SOURCEY_RESOURCES`), so `checkPermissionAsync` ignores the sourceId for it. The working gate is `nodes:read` on the body's source, the same pair `POST /security/nodes/clear` already uses. The digest handler now reads `scopedSourceId`, and a request with no `sourceId` gets 400 `MISSING_SOURCE_ID` instead of sending to

title: fix(poll): 4.17.3 review P2 Poll — sections fail on their own, slow retry while down, error notice
body:
Refs #6342 (meshtasticd 2.8.3: empty Nodes, Map and Channels while Packet Monitor and Virtual Node work). Root cause is not confirmed, so this does not close it. These fixes remove the ways one failure blanks every list with no retry and no message.

## H3 — one throw blanked the whole `/api/poll`
**What was wrong:** the grant load (`loadNodeViewAccess` / `getUserReadableVirtualChannelIds`), the node load (`getAllNodesAsync` / `loadVisibleNodesAcrossSources`), `getDeviceNodeNums` and the delta serialiser ran outside the per-section try blocks. Any throw there returned 500 for the whole reply, and the client then held no nodes and no channels.

**Fix (`src/server/routes/pollRoutes.ts`):**
- Node load: own try. On failure `nodes: []`, private-position view off, per-source visible sets cleared (they may be half filled). Other sections still answer.
- Grant load: a failed `loadNodeViewAccess` falls back to the no-user access, which is built in memory, so it can't throw again and it fails closed. A failed virtual-channel read becomes an empty set.
- `deviceNodeNums`: own try, `[]` on failure.
- Delta path: on any throw it sends the full `res.json(result)`. That reply has no `pollCursor`, so the client drops its base and asks for a full reply next time, which resets the tracker.
- Every section logs once through one helper, naming the section and the source id.
- Reply shape unchanged (no new keys). The outer 500 now uses `fail(res, 500, 'INTERNAL_ERROR', ...)`, which still sends `error`.

**Test:** `pollRoutes.sectionIsolation.test.ts` (route harness). Node read throws: 200, channels still present. Delta tracker throws: full reply with no cursor, then the next read goes back through the tracker. Grant read throws: 200, no-user view. All three fail on the old code.

## M6 — a not-connected source never re-polled after a failed first read
**What was wrong:** since a762d21d5, `usePoll` turns its interval off whenever App's status is not `connected`. If the mount read failed, or the source stayed in `configuring` / `node-offline`, nothing read the poll again and the page stayed blank.

**Fix (`src/hooks/usePoll.ts`):** while not connected, the query retries every `NOT_CONNECTED_RETRY_INTERVAL` (15 s) as long as it holds no reply or its last read failed. It stops once a read succeeds. A source that holds data still does not poll while down, so the intent of a762d21d5 holds. `App.tsx`'s connection loop was not changed. No other code seeds the poll cache while it is empty (`mergeConnectionIntoPollCache` and the WebSocket writers return early), so the retry can't switch off early.

**Test:** `usePoll.connectionGate.test.ts`: a failed first read while disconnected makes no 5 s reads, retries at 15 s, stops after a success, and makes no reads after that. The existing "reads once on mount" test passes unchanged.

title: fix(restore): skip startup retention purges on the boot that restores a backup (#6354)
body:
Closes #6354

## What
On the boot that performs a system restore (`RESTORE_FROM_BACKUP`), the **startup** run of each data-retention purge is skipped and logs a warning that names the retention window and says the next scheduled purge will remove older rows. Scheduled purges run as normal.

## Why
Restoring a backup older than the telemetry window (7 days) lost all of its telemetry: the startup purge ran 5s after boot and deleted every restored row as "older than 168h" (540,328 rows from a 13-day-old backup in a dev test). Skipping the first run gives the admin until the next scheduled purge to export the data or raise retention.

## How
- New `src/server/services/restoreBootState.ts`: an in-process "restored this boot" flag (not persisted) plus `skipStartupPurgeAfterRestore(job, window, nextRun)`. `systemRestoreService.markRestoreStarted()` / `markRestoreComplete()` open and close the boot restore check; a successful `restoreFromBackup()` sets the flag.
- Startup purges wait for that check before deciding, so they also no longer race a restore still writing rows.
- Telemetry purge timers move from `server.ts` into `telemetryPurgeSchedule.ts` so the startup/scheduled split is testable. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged.

### Startup purges now skipped on a restore boot
| Purge | Startup run | Scheduled run (unchanged) |
|---|---|---|
| Telemetry (`purgeOldTelemetryAsync`, 168h / favorites per-source) | 5s after boot | hourly |
| Coverage Report receptions + cross-source links (`coverageRetentionService`) | 30s after start | hourly |
| MeshCore position history (`meshcorePositionHistoryService`) | 30s after boot | hourly |
| Translation cache prune (`translationCacheService`) | 30s after start | hourly |

### Checked and left alone (no startup run)
- Messages, traceroutes, route segments, neighbor info, audit log, MeshCore CLI history: `databaseMaintenanceService` runs at a configured time of day, not at boot.
- Meshtastic / MeshCore / MQTT packet logs, ATAK contacts: 15-minute interval only.
- MeshCore hop SNR / trace runs (90 d): pruned on trace ingest, not at boot.
- Aircraft age-out: first tick 5 min after boot, gated on a DB-persisted last-run time; it ages out nodes rather than purging history.

## Tests
- `restoreBootState.test.ts`: no check / normal boot do not skip; restore boot skips and warns with the window; waits for an in-progress restore.
- `telemetryPurgeSchedule.test.ts`: normal boot purges at 5s; restore boot skips the 5s run and warns; hourly run purges on a restore boot (fake timers).
- `coverageRetentionService.test.ts`: restore boot skips the 30s sweep, hourly sweep runs.
- `meshcorePositionHistoryService.restore.test.ts`: startup sweep skipped on restore boot, `runCleanup` still purges.
- `systemRestoreService.test.ts`: successful restore sets the flag; failed restore does not.
- Targeted vitest: 6 files, 94 tests pass. `tsc` (server + tests projects) clean. `npm run lint:ci` OK, no FAIL lines.

title: fix(dashboard): connection banner names the viewed source's host:port (#6353)
body:
Closes #6353

## What
- `api.getConfig(sourceId?)` now reads `/api/config?sourceId=…`. App passes the viewed source, so its stored node address is that source's own host (empty for MeshCore/MQTT sources, whose config has no TCP host).
- App keeps the source's TCP port from the same config and builds the banner from two new helpers in `src/hooks/connectionCheck.ts`:
  - `formatNodeAddress(host, port)` returns `host:port` (brackets a bare IPv6 host, keeps a host that already names a port), or `''` when the host is unknown.
  - `cannotConnectMessage(address)` drops the "at <address>" phrase when the address is empty.

## Why
App called `/api/config` with no `sourceId`, which `resolveSourceConnectionConfig` answers with the env default (`192.168.1.100`). When `/api/connection` returns no `nodeIp` (a named source with no registered manager, an MQTT source that reports `''`, or a MeshCore source), the banner fell back to that env address instead of the viewed source's host.

## Permissions
No server change. `/api/config` already scopes the host and port to the named source and returns them only to callers with `sources:read` (or admin), the same rule `/api/connection` uses for `nodeIp`. A caller without it gets no host, so the banner shows no address.

## Tests
- `src/hooks/connectionCheck.test.ts`: tests for `formatNodeAddress` (host:port, existing port, IPv6, unknown port, unknown host / `Loading...`) and `cannotConnectMessage` (with and without an address).
- `src/services/api.test.ts`: `getConfig` scopes to the given source and stays unscoped with none.
- Both files pass (97 tests). `tsc -p tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.tests.json` are clean. `lint:ci` reports no in-repo FAIL lines.

title: fix(backup): skip backup columns the target table lacks on restore (#6350)
body:
Closes #6350

## What
- `systemRestoreService` now reads each table's live columns before its INSERT: `PRAGMA table_info` on SQLite, `information_schema.columns` on PostgreSQL, `information_schema.COLUMNS` on MySQL. The PG/MySQL column query replaces the old table-exists check (no columns = table absent, skipped with a warning as before). SQLite now skips a missing table the same way.
- A new `RestoreColumnFilter` inserts only the backup columns the table has, and warns once per table with every skipped name, e.g. `Restore of user_map_preferences: skipped backup column(s) the table does not have: showAccuracyRegions, sortBy, ...`.
- The column choice is per row, not first-row-only. Rows with different key sets each insert what they carry; SQLite caches one statement per column set; PG/MySQL flush a batch when the set changes. A column a row omits takes the table default. Columns follow live-table order, so key order in the file does not matter.
- SQLite and MySQL match names case-insensitively (as those engines do), without naming a column twice; PostgreSQL matches exactly (quoted identifiers).
- Unchanged: every backup key is still checked against `BACKUP_IDENTIFIER_PATTERN` (a crafted name still rolls the restore back), and a row with no column the table has still fails the restore (the all-or-nothing tests rely on this). Backup format is unchanged.

## Why
A backup from a long-lived SQLite install holds legacy camelCase columns (`showAccuracyRegions`, `showMeshCoreNodes`, ...) next to the snake_case ones. A fresh install has only snake_case, so the INSERT threw `table user_map_preferences has no column named showAccuracyRegions` and the restore aborted. The snake_case column is authoritative, so dropping the camelCase twin loses nothing.

## Tests
- `systemRestoreService.test.ts`: new `RestoreColumnFilter` unit tests (intersection, live order, per-row sets, one warning per table, case rules, identifier rejection, no-known-column rejection); coverage_receptions mocks now supply `PRAGMA table_info` rows.
- `systemBackupRestore.roundTrip.test.ts` (SQLite, real DB): restores `user_map_preferences` rows carrying legacy camelCase keys, differing key sets, and reversed key order; checks snake_case values win, an omitted column gets its default, and one warning lists the skipped columns.
- `systemBackupRestore.roundTrip.pgmysql.test.ts`: same case on PostgreSQL and MySQL (isolated databases).
- Ran 6 restore/backup files with the PG and MySQL containers up: 83/83 passed, 0 skipped. `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` clean; `npm run lint:ci` clean.

title: feat(dashboard): per-widget fixed Y-axis min/max on telemetry charts (#6348)
body:
Closes #6348.

## What
Telemetry chart widgets get a fixed Y-axis min/max. A ruler button (chart mode, editors only) opens Y min / Y max fields with Apply and Reset to auto. A blank field means auto for that end. When both are set, min must be below max. Values outside the range clip (`allowDataOverflow`).

Bounds are stored in the series' base unit (°C, A, W), the same rule the gauge range uses, so a °F display or an A→mA auto-scale doesn't move them. The editor shows them in the unit on screen.

## Where it's saved
- **Per-source Dashboard (`TelemetryChart`):** new per-source setting `dashboardChartYRange`, JSON keyed `${nodeId}-${telemetryType}`, saved the same way as `dashboardSolarVisibility`. Added to `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS`. `settingsRoutes.ts` returns 400 `INVALID_CHART_Y_RANGE` when the value isn't a JSON object, and drops non-finite bounds and min >= max pairs before storing.
- **Cross-source Telemetry page (`CombinedTelemetryChart`):** localStorage key `unifiedTelemetryYRanges`, matching how the page keeps its time range. These ranges don't sync between devices.

title: feat(mqtt): opt-in live refresh of the root finder's community directory (#6337)
body:
Closes #6337.

## Summary
- **Off by default.** A new global, admin-only setting `mqttRootDirectoryRefreshEnabled` lets the MQTT root finder refresh its community root list from `https://api.meshtastic.org/resource/mqttRoots`. The list has the same shape as our bundled copy.
- **When it fetches.** Only after a Meshtastic finder sample starts successfully, with the setting on. Never at import, at boot or on a timer.
- **How it fetches:**
  - 24 h in-memory cache, 1 h backoff after a failure, one shared in-flight request.
  - `safeFetch` with `redirect: 'error'` and a 10 s timeout.
  - Body capped at 256 KB, checked on Content-Length and while streaming.
  - ETag and 304 support.
- **Validation (`validateDirectory`).** Bad entries are dropped. The whole document is rejected if it has no valid entry or more than half are bad. Entries replace the bundled list as a whole; an empty section falls back to the bundled one. The bundled copy is always the fallback.
- **New entry form.** Entries listing `subdivisions` (from design#167) are supported, and `ladder.ts` no longer assumes every entry has a `center`.
- **UI.**
  - Settings: an admin toggle next to Elevation. Its help text says the request reveals only the server's IP and the time someone used the finder.
  - Finder: a footnote shows "bundled copy" or "updated <date>".

## Mesh impact
None. No RF. The only outbound call is one bare HTTPS GET at most every 24 h, and only when an admin has turned it on and someone uses the finder.

## Notes
- **Setting read.** The route reads the setting and passes it to the provider, because `isolation.test.ts` forbids database imports under `mqttRootFinder/`.
- **Turning it off.** A live copy fetched earlier stays in use until the next finder start or a restart.

## Testing
- Server and frontend `tsc` and the lint ratchet are clean.
- Directory, provider, ladder, isolation, route, settings and UI suites pass, all with the network mocked.

title: feat(mqtt): offline geocoder for root finder subdivision and city rows (#6336)
body:
Closes #6336.

## Summary
- **Offline reverse geocoder** (`src/server/services/offlineGeocoder/`), so the MQTT root finder can fill its subdivision and city rows (R4–R6 of #6287). Same coordinate, same ladder; no network lookup.
- **Data** (manual refresh, pinned by version and sha256 in `geoDataVersion.ts`; rebuilt reproducibly by `scripts/geo/build-offline-geocoder.ts`):
  - Natural Earth 10m admin-1 v5.1.2 (public domain), merged to top-level ISO 3166-2 for GB, FR, IT, ES, BE, IE and PH.
  - GeoNames `cities15000` (CC BY 4.0), in its own module so it can be dropped. Credit is in `THIRD_PARTY_DATA.md`.
- **Lookup:** typed-array point-in-polygon (even-odd over all rings), with a 10 km nearest-edge fallback for coasts. Ties go to the lowest code.
- **City pick:** lowest distance ÷ √population within 15 km. This returns "Paris", not "Paris 04 Hôtel-de-Ville". Neighbourhoods and historical places are excluded.
- **Wiring:** an injectable geocoder resolves the place once, in `start()`. Meshtastic only: MeshCore samples (#6343) skip it. Coordinates are never logged or returned.

## Sizes and cost
| | gz | base64 in source |
|---|---|---|
| admin1 (3,845 features, 207k vertices, simplified 15%) | 955 KiB | 1,274 KiB |
| cities (31,789) | 467 KiB | 624 KiB |
| **Total** | **1.42 MiB** | **1.90 MiB** |

- At 15% simplification, 0.52% of places land in a different subdivision than they do with unsimplified data.
- Decoding takes about 30 ms and holds about 4 MB, freed after 10 min idle. A lookup takes about 9 µs.
- Server `tsc` time is unchanged. The data modules export a plain string, so tsc builds no literal type.
- The desktop workflow now asserts that the data files are in `dist`.

## Mesh impact
None. The geocoder is a local lookup with no RF and no network.

## Testing
- 166 tests passed across the finder, routes and geocoder suites.
- Covered:
  - real-data cases: Seattle, Texarkana tier 2, Kiel → `DE/SH`, Edinburgh → GB-SCT, Paris → FR-IDF, Lesotho enclave, offshore Miami, mid-Atlantic, antimeridian;
  - a seeded 200-point snapshot;
  - performance and memory bounds;
  - privacy: no lat/lon in responses;
  - isolation: no fs, net or child_process imports.
- Server and frontend `tsc` and the lint ratchet are clean.

title: fix(mqtt): reject invalid MQTT root topics server-side on save (#6338)
body:
Closes #6338.

## Summary
- **Server-side check for MQTT root topics.** The server now refuses an invalid root, but **only when the root changes**. An unknown previous root counts as changed. Paths covered:
  - `POST /api/config/mqtt`
  - remote-admin `setMQTTConfig`, for local and remote nodes
  - saved broker presets
  - the embedded broker's `rootTopic`, where `''` is refused
- **Shared helper.** `src/server/utils/mqttRootGuard.ts` builds on the existing `validateMqttRoot` (31-byte firmware limit, wildcards, whitespace, control and invisible characters, bad slashes, trailing `/2`). A refusal returns `fail(400, 'INVALID_MQTT_ROOT', msg, { field, reason })`.
- **Existing bad roots don't block unrelated edits.** Firmware resends the whole MQTT struct on every save, so an unchanged root is left alone.
- **Restores are applied as before.** Device restore logs a warning and adds a new optional `RestoreResult.warnings[]` entry.
- **UI:**
  - The error shows in your language through `ApiError` `code`/`reason` and the existing `mqtt_root_finder.validation.*` strings.
  - Save is disabled when the root has changed and is invalid: device MQTT form, remote-admin form and preset dialogs.

## Mesh impact
None. This only refuses saves. It adds no sends, timers or notifications.

## Testing
- Server and frontend `tsc` are clean, and the lint ratchet is OK.
- 165 new or changed tests, all on `createRouteTestApp` for routes. More than 300 existing tests were re-run across config, admin, backup, SaveBar and MQTT round-trip suites.
- Not done: a browser check (jsdom only). There are no schema changes, so no PG/MySQL run was needed.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

diff:
--- docs/internal/dev-notes/ISSUE_6338_SPEC.md (+106/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,106 @@
+## Maintainer decisions (2026-11-10, binding)
+Reject only when the root changes (an unknown previous value counts as changed). Enforce on POST /config/mqtt, remote-admin setMQTTConfig, broker presets and the embedded-broker rootTopic (reject empty there) with fail(400, 'INVALID_MQTT_ROOT', msg, {field, reason}). Restores stay verbatim with a logged warning (add warnings[] to RestoreResult). No normalisation on device saves. Localise the error in the UI via ApiError code/reason and disable Save on a changed invalid root.
+
+# Spec: #6338, reject invalid MQTT root topics server-side
+
+## Findings
+- **Validator.** `src/utils/mqttRootTopic.ts:9` sets `MAX_ROOT_BYTES = 31`. `validateMqttRoot` at `:33-47` returns `WHITESPACE | CONTROL | INVISIBLE | WILDCARD | SLASH | ENDS_WITH_2 | TOO_LONG`, and `''` is valid (firmware default). It is already imported server-side (`src/server/utils/mqttRootFinderTarget.ts:27,64`, `src/server/services/mqttRootFinder/ladder.ts:191`), so it is safe to reuse in the server.
+- **en.json.** It has all seven `mqtt_root_finder.validation.<CODE>` strings.
+- **Firmware limit.** `protobufs/meshtastic/module_config.options:6` has `*MQTTConfig.root max_size:32`. Usable is 32-1 = 31 bytes, so `MAX_ROOT_BYTES` already matches firmware.
+- **UI is advisory only.** `src/components/MQTT/MqttRootFieldError.tsx:1-3` says "UI only: the server does not reject a root on save". It is used in `MQTTConfigSection.tsx:627`, `ModuleConfigurationSection.tsx:363`, `SavedBrokerPresetDialogs.tsx:159`, and in warn mode at `MqttBridgeConfigurationView.tsx:703`. No form disables Save.
+
+### Server paths that save a root, and what they check today
+| Path | Location | Current check |
+|---|---|---|
+| Local device `POST /api/config/mqtt` | `src/server/routes/configRoutes.ts:247-260` | None. Only `fillDeviceMqttFromPreset`, then `setMQTTConfig` (`deviceAdminService.ts:275-292`, firmware replaces the whole struct). |
+| Remote admin `setMQTTConfig` | `src/server/routes/adminRoutes.ts:2124-2134` | Checks only that `config` is present, plus the preset fill. |
+| Saved broker presets (`rootTopic`; applied to the device `root` at `src/components/MQTT/brokerPresets.ts:242`) | `src/server/routes/mqttBrokerPresetRoutes.ts:110-115` | Weak. Trims, strips trailing `/`, rejects `#`, `+` and whitespace. Allows control and invisible characters, leading `/`, `//`, `/2`, and more than 31 bytes. Errors are `{error}` only. |
+| Embedded broker source `mqtt_broker.rootTopic` | Type at `src/server/mqttBrokerManager.ts:43`. Used as a prefix at `:165` and `:425` (`(rootTopic ?? 'msh') + '/'`). Create at `sourceRoutes.ts:1021-1027`, update at `:1329-1336`. | None. A `''`, trailing `/` or wildcard root silently breaks the prefix match. The UI does not edit this field (API only), and it is shown at `sourceConfigRedaction.ts:531`. |
+| MQTT bridge sources | `subscriptions` are topic filters (wildcards are legal) | Out of scope. The UI only warns, which is correct. |
+| MeshCore MQTT | Fixed `meshcore/{IATA}/…`. IATA is validated at `sourceRoutes.ts:385-390`. | No root. Out of scope. |
+| First-boot env vars | None found for an MQTT root (grep of `src/server/config/*Env.ts` and `process.env.*MQTT`) | N/A |
+| Device config restore (#4926) | `backupRoutes.ts:168-205`, then `deviceRestoreService.ts:207-208` calls `manager.setMQTTConfig(moduleConfig.mqtt)` directly, bypassing the routes. It is best-effort per section; failures go to `failed[]`. | None (verbatim by design). |
+| System restore | Copies `sources` (`systemBackupTables.ts:40`) and `mqtt_broker_presets` (`:176`) table-wide. | None (only archive validation). |
+
+### Previous root, for checking only changed values
+- **Local node:** `manager.getActualModuleConfig()?.mqtt?.root`. The same read is used at `deviceAdminService.ts:638`.
+- **Remote node:** `manager.getRemoteNodeConfig(nodeNum)?.moduleConfig?.mqtt?.root` (`meshtasticManager.ts:6299`). The remote-admin form refuses Save until it has loaded the node's config (`AdminCommandsTab.tsx:1329-1339`), so this cache is normally filled.
+- **Preset:** the stored row, already loaded as `stored` in the preset parser.
+- **Broker source:** `existing.config.rootTopic` in PUT.
+
+### How the UI shows errors today
+- `apiService.setMQTTConfig` (`src/services/api.ts:1845-1858`) throws `new Error(body.error)` and drops `code`. `ConfigurationTab.tsx:1173-1177` shows `mqtt_failed: <message>` in a toast.
+- The admin `executeCommand` shows `error.message` in a toast (`AdminCommandsTab.tsx:~998-1006`).
+- Result: the server's message text is what users see.
+
+## Which paths to enforce on
+1. `POST /api/config/mqtt` and admin `setMQTTConfig`: enforce, only when the root changes (see the next section).
+2. Broker preset create/update: replace the ad-hoc regex with `validateMqttRoot`, applied after the existing trim and trailing-slash strip. Enforce only when it differs from `stored.rootTopic`. A new preset always counts as a change.
+3. `mqtt_broker` source create/update: validate `rootTopic` when present and changed. Also reject `''`, because `''` means "firmware default" for a device but here it produces the prefix `/`.
+4. Device restore and system restore: do not reject. Restore is verbatim by #4926 design, and refusing a whole archive or MQTT section because of an old root is worse than restoring it. In `deviceRestoreService`, log a `logger.warn` and add a non-fatal note (e.g. a `warnings[]` entry in `RestoreResult`, if the maintainer agrees).
+5. Bridge, MeshCore and env vars: nothing to do.
+
+Put the logic in one helper, `src/server/utils/mqttRootGuard.ts`:
+```ts
+checkMqttRootSave(next: unknown, prev: unknown, opts?: { allowEmpty?: boolean })
+  : null | { code: 'INVALID_MQTT_ROOT'; reason: MqttRootErrorCode | 'NOT_STRING' | 'EMPTY'; message: string }
+```
+Rules:
+- `undefined` → valid (proto default `''`).
+- A non-string → `NOT_STRING`.
+- `next === prev` → valid, skipped.
+- Otherwise run `validateMqttRoot`.
+
+`message` comes from a small server-side English map that copies the en.json wording.
+
+## Existing invalid saved configs
+- **Reject only when the root changes (recommended).** Unrelated edits still save, e.g. toggling map reporting on a node that already has `msh/US ` or a 40-byte root. This matters because firmware replaces the whole struct, so every save resends the root. Restores are not affected. The user can't save a new bad root. Cost: a stored bad root can stay until someone edits it. If the previous value is unknown (no cache), treat the root as changed and validate it.
+- **Reject always.** Strictest. It blocks every MQTT edit on any node or preset that already holds a bad root, including roots set by the Meshtastic app or CLI, until the root is fixed. If also applied to restore, it would fail the whole `module.mqtt` section, so old backups would restore without MQTT. It would also block system restores containing such presets or sources.
+- **Warn only.** Returns `ok` with `warnings: [{ field: 'root', reason }]`. It never blocks, so it does not meet the issue's goal. It is only suitable for restore paths.
+
+## Error envelope
+```ts
+return fail(res, 400, 'INVALID_MQTT_ROOT', err.message, { field: 'root' /* or 'rootTopic' */, reason: err.reason });
+```
+- Run it after `fillDeviceMqttFromPreset` in `configRoutes.ts` and before `buildAdminMessage` in `adminRoutes.ts`. Presets and sources should also use `fail()` for this code, even though their neighbouring checks still return `{error}`.
+- **UI, minimal:** nothing to change. The English `message` appears in the existing toasts.
+- **UI, recommended:** change `apiService.setMQTTConfig` to throw `ApiError(message, status, { code, body })`. Callers then map `code === 'INVALID_MQTT_ROOT'` to `t(\`mqtt_root_finder.validation.${body.reason}\`)` so the message is localized. Add `NOT_STRING`/`EMPTY` keys, or fall back to `message`.
+- Update the comment in `MqttRootFieldError.tsx:1-3`.
+- Optional: disable Save when the root has changed and is invalid, mirroring the server.
+
+## Test plan
+Use `createRouteTestApp` (`src/server/test-helpers/routeTestApp.ts`) and mock the device manager as `configRoutes.test.ts` does.
+- **`configRoutes.mqttRoot.test.ts`:**
+  - One case per code (`'msh /US'`, `'msh\u0007'`, `'msh\u200B'`, `'msh/#'`, `'/msh'`, `'msh//US'`, `'msh/US/2'`, a 32-byte root and a 31-byte multi-byte root) → 400 `{success:false, code:'INVALID_MQTT_ROOT', reason}`, and `setMQTTConfig` is not called.
+  - `''` and `'msh/US/FL'` → 200.
+  - Cached root already invalid, same root resubmitted with `mapReportingEnabled` toggled → 200 (unrelated edit passes).
+  - Changed to another invalid root → 400.
+  - No cached config → validated.

title: feat(meshcore): IATA region finder for MeshCore MQTT ingest (#6335)
body:
Closes #6335.

## Summary
- A **Find regions** button under the Region (IATA) field of the MeshCore MQTT ingest form. It lists the regions that have observers online on the broker; **Use this** fills the field (upper-cased) and nothing is saved.
- New `meshcoreRegionAdapter` for the shared #6287 root finder. It subscribes to the single filter `meshcore/+/+/status` for 60 s, with no `#`.
- An observer counts as active when its status is `online` and either the timestamp is under 15 minutes old or the message arrived live. Regions are ranked by active observers, then status messages, then code. There is no ladder, community list or distance.
- One shared implementation: the service picks the adapter by protocol, and the same hook and `MqttRootFinder` component switch copy and sections. The Meshtastic finder is unchanged.
- The `meshcore_mqtt` context needs `sources:write` on the source. A stored login is reused only on the same broker endpoint. The form's TLS-verify checkbox is honoured. A MeshCore-specific hint is shown on `SUBSCRIBE_DENIED`.
- Adapters now receive a `{ retained }` flag, needed for the "arrived live" rule. The Meshtastic adapter ignores it.

## Mesh impact
None. The finder only subscribes to the broker and sends no RF, DB writes, events or publishes. Every #6287 cap is reused unchanged: 60 s sample, 1 per user, 1 per endpoint, 2 instance-wide, 2 min cooldown, 5 starts per 10 min. `isolation.test.ts` asserts zero publishes and no manager imports.

## Testing
- Server and frontend `tsc` and the lint ratchet are clean.
- Finder server tests 77/77; routes + component 45/45; Dashboard fieldset 12/12.
- Not done: a browser check against a live MeshCore broker.

title: feat(automation): Meshtastic long-message split through the shared splitter (#6330)
body:
Closes #6330.

## Summary
- One shared split runner for both protocols (`src/server/utils/automatedTextSplit.ts`, limits in `src/utils/messageSplitLimits.ts`): 200-byte parts on Meshtastic, at most 3 parts, `(i/N)` markers, 10 s gap, per-source mutex. A cut part ends in "..." on both protocols. **This changes MeshCore**, which cut silently before.
- **Auto Responder Multiline** on Meshtastic now uses the shared splitter. It sends at most 3 marked parts; before, it had no part cap and no markers.
- **Timer Triggers, Auto Announce and the Automation Engine send action** on Meshtastic gain the opt-in "Split long messages" option. It is off by default; off means the text is cut to 200 bytes with "...". A split timer must fire at most every 5 minutes; the server rejects a shorter interval with `SPLIT_TIMER_INTERVAL_TOO_SHORT`.
- **Skip if still queued:** a Timer Trigger or scheduled Auto Announce fire is skipped (logged at info) while items from its previous fire are still being sent or are still in the message queue. This applies with split on or off. The manual "Send Announcement" button is never skipped.
- Behaviour change: Meshtastic Auto Announce with split off now cuts to 200 bytes with "..." (it used to hand the full text to the radio).

## Mesh impact
- **Airtime:** a full 200-byte part takes about 2.0 s on LongFast and about 0.6 s on MediumFast. Three parts are about 6 s from our node, or about 24 s across the mesh at hop limit 3.
- **Bounds:**
  - Responder, timer and announce parts go through the per-source queue, which sends one item every 30 s, so our node stays at most ~7% duty on LongFast.
  - Each timer, and each source's announce, has at most one fire in the queue. For example, an 8-channel split timer at the 5-minute floor (24 items, about 12 min to send) fires about every 15 min instead of piling up.
  - The Automation Engine channel path sends direct with a 10 s gap. Its `rateLimit` caps fires, not parts.
- **Spam:** Multiline replies drop from unlimited parts to at most 3. Split is off by default everywhere new. Saving settings re-arms no timer.
- All limits are maintainer decisions recorded on #6330.

- Server and frontend `tsc` are clean, and `lint-ratchet` is OK.
- Targeted Vitest: server, 24 files, 422 passed; frontend, 14 files, 198 passed (the 60 skipped are an existing `describe.skip`).
- Not done: live deploy, browser check, system tests.

title: feat(automation): MeshCore confirmed new-neighbour alert (#6274)
body:
Closes #6274.

## Summary
- New automation trigger `trigger.neighborAdded`: fires when a MeshCore repeater's neighbour table gains a node that is still listed after a set time (`confirmHours`, default 72, range 6–336).
- Migration 230 adds `meshcore_neighbor_watch` (per-source) on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL. It tracks pending neighbours with first-seen and last-heard times. Entries go stale after 24 h, are dropped after 7 days with no sighting, and are pruned after 30 days.
- The rule decides on each sighting whether it crosses its own `confirmHours` (`prevLastHeardAt - firstSeenAt < H <= lastHeardAt - firstSeenAt`). Each rule fires once per episode with no per-rule state, so a restart or a settings save cannot re-fire it.
- Device Health template: new "confirmed new neighbour" alert with an optional minimum-SNR filter, capped at 5 alerts per hour.
- Docs: automation engine page and the issue spec.

## Mesh impact
- **Airtime:** none. The trigger reads neighbour tables MeshMonitor already polls and sends nothing.
- **Spam:** notifications only. The template caps them at 5 per hour. The self-origin guard (#3914) drops a neighbour that is our own key.
- **Timers:** confirmation is computed from stored timestamps, so restarts and saves don't reset it.
- **Limitation:** a Companion source only lists its 10 strongest neighbours per poll (documented).

## Testing
- Server and frontend `tsc` are clean after merging main (#6273 conflicts resolved by keeping both triggers).
- Targeted Vitest run: 1320 tests passed (gates, neighborAdded, neighborWatch, templates).

title: feat(meshcore): show stored room posts read-only without a live login (#6332)
body:
Closes #6332.

A room server pushes new posts to every client in its access list, and MeshMonitor stores them whenever the companion receives them, independent of a login in the UI. The Rooms view still hid those stored posts behind a full login overlay, so a room could list 25 posts that nobody could read if the login timed out.

## What it does
- When the selected room is not logged in, its stored posts render read-only (the shared `MeshCoreMessageStream` with `hideComposer`), under a compact banner: "Not logged in — showing saved posts. Log in to post or fetch new ones." The banner holds the existing login controls (password, Remember, Login, Forget saved password, #6267 Auto-sync).
- Composer and the stats/sync header stay login-only. Auto-login with a saved password is unchanged.
- A login that times out now explains the protocol: a room server sends **no reply** when it refuses a login, so a timeout usually means this radio is no longer in the room's access list, a guest password is needed (or read-only guests are not allowed), or the room is out of range.

## Mesh impact
None: the history read was already made on select; no new requests, no RF.

## Tests
New `MeshCoreRoomsView.readOnly.test.tsx`: logged-out posts + banner + controls, no composer/stats; posts and hint stay after a no-reply failure; logged-in view unchanged. Rooms view suites + semantic tokens: 59 passed; type checks and lint ratchet clean.

title: feat(meshcore): optional senderName for API channel sends, per-source allowlist (#6282)
body:
Closes #6282. Spec and maintainer decisions: `docs/internal/dev-notes/ISSUE_6282_SPEC.md`.

## What it does
API callers may send a MeshCore channel message under an **allowed** sender name (`senderName` on `POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/messages/send` and v1 `POST /messages`).
- **Off by default.** Per-source setting edited with `configuration:write` ("API sender names" card in Device Configuration, Companion only, with an impersonation warning): enable + up to 16 allowed names. Callers need their existing send grants **and** a listed name (403 `SENDER_NAME_DISABLED` / `SENDER_NAME_NOT_ALLOWED`). A name equal to the node's own name takes the normal path.
- Names: 1–31 bytes, NFC, no `:`, control, bidi or zero-width characters, no leading `#`.
- Sent as a raw `GRP_TXT` flood via `CMD_SEND_RAW_PACKET` (companion firmware ≥ v1.16 / version code 13; older → 422). Scope mirrors the firmware's `sendFloodScoped`, including the node's own default region (`CMD_GET_DEFAULT_FLOOD_SCOPE`). Text cap is 5 bytes lower than a normal send (`155 − name − 2`) because of the 176-byte frame limit. Refused (409) when the companion has client repeat on or the channel key is missing.
- **Echo safety:** the radio does not mark a raw send as seen, so its own echo would arrive as a stranger's message. That copy is dropped for 10 minutes; heard-repeater matching compares the exact payload; a process-wide registry of recent override names makes sibling sources treat the echo as `selfOrigin`, so Auto-Ack, Auto-Responder and Forwarding never reply to it.
- **Resend** rebuilds the same raw packet (same bytes, so repeaters drop duplicates) and never falls back to the real node name.
- **Audit:** every override send (`meshcore_message_sent_as`, no message text), denials, and allowlist changes. API-token callers are now attributed in MeshCore audit rows.
- Migration 230 (SQLite/PostgreSQL/MySQL): nullable `meshcore_messages.senderNameOverride`; own bubbles show "Sent as X".

## Mesh impact
Same airtime as a normal channel send (one flood packet, same 160-byte budget); no timers, no retries; existing message rate limits apply. Automations cannot set a sender name in this version.

## Security
Impersonation risk is real (GRP_TXT has no sender authentication), hence default-off, admin-curated allowlist, and full audit.

## Tests
Frame builder (golden vectors, ≤176 bytes), name validator, native raw-packet and default-scope commands (version gate, error mapping, receive-only blocked), manager (scope modes, stored row, echo suppression, sibling self-origin, raw resend, client-repeat refusal), migration on all three backends, routes with the real harness (DM/Meshtastic 400, disabled/unlisted 403, caps, old firmware 422, audit), UI card and label. Final broad run: 37,348 passed, 0 failed, no PG/MySQL skips. Not tried on a real radio.

## Note
Migration 230 also used by #6274's branch; whichever merges second renumbers.

title: feat(meshcore): split long messages in Auto Responder, Timer Triggers, Auto Announce and automations (#6316)
body:
Closes #6316. Spec and maintainer decisions: `docs/internal/dev-notes/ISSUE_6316_SPEC.md`.

## What it does
- One shared sender, `MeshCoreManager.sendAutomatedText`, used by Auto Ack (refactored, behaviour unchanged), **Auto Responder** (new per-trigger *multiline* toggle), **Timer Triggers** (per-timer toggle), **Auto Announce** (new per-source setting) and the **Automation Engine** send-message action (new *Split long messages* checkbox, MeshCore only).
- Text is fitted to the firmware cap from #6303 (DM 160, channel 160 − name − 2). With split on: at most **3 parts** marked `(i/N)`, **10 s apart**, sent part by part across the target channels; a **per-source mutex** keeps sequences from interleaving; a failed target is dropped from later parts; it stops on receive-only.
- With split off, all four senders now **truncate to the cap** app-side, so the stored row matches what went on air (no extra packets; previously the firmware cut channel text silently).
- Scripts split only when they emit exactly one message.
- One shared UI field (`SplitLongMessagesField`) with the airtime warning.

## Mesh impact (maintainer-chosen limits)
Each part is a full flood packet (~0.63 s airtime on the US preset, ~1.7 s on EU narrow, × every repeater in range). Limits: max 3 parts, fixed 10 s gap, per-source mutex, chat parts do not stamp `recordMeshTx`, and a **split-enabled timer must be at least 5 minutes apart** (enforced server-side: 400 `SPLIT_TIMER_INTERVAL_TOO_SHORT`, plus a UI warning). Worst case without that floor would have been 12 sends/min (34% duty on EU narrow).

## Tests
Planner, shared sender (part order, gap outside the lock, receive-only mid-sequence, failed target dropped, stored text = sent text), responder/timer/announce split, timer guard and route 400, automation action pass-through, UI field. Existing `autoAckSplit.test.ts` unchanged and green. Targeted runs: 5,289 + 2,583 passed; type checks and lint ratchet clean after merging main. Not tried on hardware.

## Release note
MeshCore Auto Responder triggers, Timer Triggers, Auto Announce and the Automation Engine send-message action can now split a long message into up to 3 marked parts, 10 seconds apart. They also cut over-long messages to the firmware limit, so the stored message matches what went on air. A timer with splitting on must be at least 5 minutes apart.

title: feat(mqtt): root topic finder — subscribe-only broker sample (#6287)
body:
Closes #6287. Spec and maintainer decisions: `docs/internal/dev-notes/ISSUE_6287_SPEC.md`. Follows meshtastic/design#167 and the Apple app's Find Topics sheet.

## What it does
A **Find topics** button next to every MQTT root field (Device Config, remote admin, bridge config, bridge create, saved presets) opens a sheet that samples the broker for **60 s** (Stop keeps partial results), subscribe-only, and lists:
- **Suggested** roots (region ladder),
- **Community** roots from a bundled, pinned copy of meshtastic/api `data/mqttRoots.json` (commit `7406a79f`, works offline),
- **Heard** roots ranked by tier, map-report distance (rounded km only), node and message count; floor badge when the region stream hit the 300-packet cap.

Picking a row fills the field; **nothing is saved** — the form's normal Save applies it. Shared root validation (`validateMqttRoot`, design#167 R8: no whitespace/control/invisible chars, no wildcards, no bad slashes, not ending in `/2`, ≤ 31 UTF-8 bytes, any script) shows under every root field.

## Mesh impact: none
One outbound subscribe-only MQTT connection to the broker the user typed. Never publishes (no LWT, `clean: true`), never ingests, never touches a radio, never writes the DB, no retries. 21 isolation tests prove it (publish spy = 0 on every path, no `will`, exactly 8 filters and never `#`, ingest/event/DB recorders at 0, static import-boundary check).

## Limits (maintainer decisions)
Max 1 active sample per user, 1 per broker endpoint, 2 instance-wide; 2-minute per-user cooldown; HTTP limiter 5 starts / 10 min (not skipped for private IPs).

## Security
- Permission = whoever can save that root: `configuration:write` on the source (device / remote), `sources:write` (bridges), admin (presets).
- SSRF: only mqtt/mqtts/ws/wss URLs or device address + TLS; `assertSafeHost` blocks metadata / link-local for everyone and loopback for non-admins; coarse error codes only (no raw broker/socket text).
- Stored bridge passwords are reused only for the same endpoint (via `mergeSourceConfigOnSave`, admins included); preset logins through the existing preset fill.
- No coordinates, passwords or raw errors in responses; location never reaches the broker.

## Known gaps (tracked as follow-ups)
No geocoder yet (phase 1): country/subdivision/city rows appear only when a place is known, so cross-client ladder parity for those rungs is not met yet. Also: MeshCore IATA finder (adapter seam is in place), live directory refresh, server-side root enforcement on save, optional `!<8-hex>` client id for strict brokers. Residual DNS-rebinding risk documented (same stance as `ssrfGuard.ts`).

## Tests
Validator, client additions, ladder/ranking (design#167 acceptance cases), sampler with fake client, routes (permissions, endpoint-bound credentials, blocked targets, caps → 429, ownership 404, no secrets in responses), isolation guard, UI sheet/hook and the five mounts. Targeted run after merging main: 347 passed (finder/MQTT/transport) plus
