title: feat(meshcore): decrypt Companion OTA GRP_TXT with virtual channel keys and show them on the Channels page (#6159)
body:
## Summary

A MeshCore **Companion** hears the raw OTA frame of every packet in range via `ota_packet` (LogRxData 0x88), including GRP_TXT on channels that are not set on its radio. Until now those frames were stored in the Packet Monitor but never decrypted against **virtual channels** in the Channel Database, so a virtual channel added no decrypt keys to a Companion and its "Decrypted packets" count stayed 0. The Repeater RAW and `meshcore_mqtt` paths already decrypt against virtual + cross-source keys; this brings the Companion `ota_packet` path in line, and surfaces the result on the Companion's Channels page.

Closes #6159.

### Part A — decrypt Companion OTA GRP_TXT against virtual / cross-source keys
- The Companion `ota_packet` branch now runs GRP_TXT frames through the **same shared `meshcoreFrameIngest` decrypt** (`decryptGroupTextFrame`) as the Repeater path, using the same key candidates: MeshCore virtual channels (#5552) plus any other source's channel key the viewer may read.
- Opened messages are filed under a **keyed channel index** derived from the secret and stamped with `keySourceId` / `keyChannelIdx` / `keyFingerprint`, exactly like the Repeater path. The repeater and companion storage logic is unified into one `storeDecryptedGroupText` helper so the two cannot drift.
- `decryptedPacketCount` is incremented via `noteVirtualChannelDecrypt` **only** for a message a virtual key actually opened.
- **Receive-only:** the path stores/emits only — it never transmits (no packets, no acks, no auto-reply/forward/ping; a test asserts those probes are never invoked).
- Per-source scoped: every row carries `sourceId`; `getKeyedChannelSummaries` is per-source.

### Dedup / double-store strategy
If a channel **is** set on the Companion, the firmware already delivers the decrypted message through the normal channel-message event. I guard with a **channel-hash check**: before decrypting, `companionHoldsChannelHash` tests the frame's channel hash against the Companion's in-memory key cache (`channelSecrets`) plus the always-present Public slot; a match means the firmware handles it, so the OTA path skips the frame (no double-store, no spurious virtual decrypt count). I chose the hash check over id-dedup because the normal channel path uses a different id scheme, so id-dedup would not catch cross-path duplicates. Only virtual / cross-source keys reach storage. (Design fork: the issue offered either approach; the hash check matches the "skip frames whose channel hash matches a key held on the device" option and is robust against the shared decrypt's same-secret candidate de-dup.)

### Part B — show virtual-channel messages on the Companion's Channels page
The existing #5551 keyed-channel machinery already runs for `meshcore` sources and is per-source + key-gated (`/api/channels/all` lists keyed channels via `listKeyedChannelsForViewer`; `/channels/:idx/messages` reads them with `resolveMeshcoreKeyAccess` + `filterKeyedMessages`). Once Part A store

title: fix(virtual-node): don't relay own want_config_id burst to VN clients (#6161)
body:
## Bug

When MeshMonitor refreshes its node database (hourly, on reconnect, or on a manual resync) it sends its own `want_config_id` to the physical node. The node answers with a config burst — `my_info`, `metadata`, `config`, `moduleConfig`, and a run of `node_info` frames. MeshMonitor relayed that whole burst to its virtual node clients, including the Meshtastic Android app.

The app never asked for that config. The `channel` and `configComplete` frames were already filtered out of the relay, so the app saw a config stream that began with no channels and never finished. It treated that as "config done with zero channels" and dropped its channel names. On the hourly refresh, the app's channel names kept disappearing.

## Fix

`sendWantConfigId()` now arms a suppression window (`VN_CONFIG_RELAY_SUPPRESS_MS`, 120s). While the window is open, the burst FromRadio types (`myInfo`, `metadata`, `config`, `moduleConfig`, `nodeInfo`) are not relayed to virtual node clients. A `configComplete` clears the window immediately; the 120s deadline bounds it if no `configComplete` ever arrives. Apps already receive the full config through the controlled `sendInitialConfig()` flow, so nothing is lost.

## Mesh impact

None. This change only *reduces* unsolicited traffic to virtual node clients. It sends nothing on the LoRa mesh and arms no new timer that fires traffic.

## Testing

- New unit test `src/server/meshtasticManager.vnConfigBurst6161.test.ts` (8 cases): each burst type is dropped after `sendWantConfigId()`; a nodeInfo relays normally with no pending request; `configComplete` clears the window so a later nodeInfo relays again; and the window is bounded by its deadline.
- `npx vitest run` on the new file: 8/8 green.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.server.json`: clean.
- `npm run lint:ci`: no in-repo failures.

Closes #6161

title: fix(virtual-node): ack-and-drop blocked addContact so app DMs don't stall 30s (#6163)
body:
## Summary

Android app DMs sent through MeshMonitor's virtual node stalled for ~30 s before actually going out. The virtual node already **blocks** `addContact` admin messages from clients (issue #1487 — forwarding them would corrupt the PKI key store on the physical node), but it did a bare `return` with no reply. The Android app's `sendAdminAwait` waits for a routing ack on the `add_contact` it sends before composing the DM, so with no ack it burned its full 30 s routing-ack timeout every time.

## The fix

**Ack-and-drop**, exactly like the existing `removeByNodenum` intercept for issue #2602 a few lines below in the same file: keep blocking `addContact`, but first fabricate a routing ack (`errorReason=NONE`) and send it back only to the requesting client. The app gets its ack immediately and sends the DM without the stall.

(Fix committed in `src/server/virtualNodeServer.ts` ~line 465; this PR adds the unit test.)

## Mesh impact

None. The fabricated ack is a FromRadio frame written only to the requesting web/app client over the local TCP socket — nothing is transmitted on the mesh. The PKI-corrupting `addContact` is still blocked and never reaches the physical node.

## Testing

- Added `src/server/virtualNodeServer.zombieFix.test.ts` coverage mirroring the #2602 tests: a blocked `addContact` is not forwarded to the physical node, and the requesting client receives a routing ack whose requestId matches the ToRadio packet id. Also asserts a non-`addContact` admin message does not fabricate an ack.
- `npx vitest run src/server/virtualNodeServer.zombieFix.test.ts` — 12/12 green.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.server.json` — clean.
- `npm run lint:ci` (worktree paths filtered) — clean.

Closes #6163

title: fix(config): Reload Config re-reads MQTT map reporting and Report Location
body:
## Problem

On Device Configuration → MQTT, **Reload Config** does not refresh the map reporting checkboxes:

- **Report Location** (`mapReportSettings.shouldReportLocation`) was never re-read on reload. If it was changed on the radio (for example from the iOS app), the page kept the old value.
- **Map Reporting** (`mapReportingEnabled`) was only updated when the field was present. proto3 leaves out `false`, so turning it off on the radio never cleared the box.

The next **Save** then sent the stale value back to the radio. With Report Location wrongly saved as off, the node's map reports carry no position, and public maps show "This node has not reported a position".

## Fix

`handleReloadConfig` now reads both flags the same way the initial load does (`=== true`, so a missing flag means off). Each change is listed in the reload summary, like the MQTT Encryption flag already is.

## Tests

`ConfigurationTab.mqttRoundTrip.test.tsx`, 2 new cases:
- Report Location turned on at the radio shows after Reload, and a Save afterwards sends it.
- A reload where both flags are elided turns both checkboxes off.

Both fail without the fix. All 10 `ConfigurationTab*` suites pass (68 tests), and `lint:ci` and `typecheck` pass.

Related: #6176 (the MQTT bridge dropped map reports), #6174 (map pin for the fixed position).

title: fix(mqtt-bridge): uplink a node's own map report instead of dropping it on the ok_to_mqtt gate
body:
## Problem

A node whose MQTT goes through MeshMonitor's built-in broker and an MQTT Bridge to a public server (for example `mqtt.meshtastic.org`) never shows a position on public maps such as meshtastic.liamcottle.net. Those maps show "This node has not reported a position", even with Map Reporting and a fixed position turned on.

## Cause

Public maps take a node's position from its **map report**. That is a `MAP_REPORT_APP` packet the firmware publishes to `msh/<region>/2/map/` from `MQTT::perhapsReportToMap`. It is sent outside `MQTT::onSend`, so it has no `Data.bitfield` and no `ok_to_mqtt` bit; the node's own **Map Reporting** setting is the opt-in.

`MqttBridgeManager.handleUplink` runs every uplink through the fail-closed `ok_to_mqtt` gate. For a map report, `resolveOkToMqttForEnvelope` returns `'unknown'` (no bitfield, not encrypted), `allowsUplink` treats that as "no", and the report is dropped and counted in `uplinkOkToMqttDrops`. Only bridges with **Uplink all packets (ignore ok_to_mqtt bit)** turned on let them through.

## Fix

- `isOwnMapReport(envelope)` in `src/server/utils/okToMqtt.ts` is true for an unencrypted `MAP_REPORT_APP` packet whose `from` is the gateway that published it, which is exactly what the firmware sends.
- The bridge skips the `ok_to_mqtt` gate for those packets only. Every other packet is gated as before, and the topic/channel/node/portnum filters, echo suppression, automation drop and cross-bridge relay check all still run first.
- A map report relayed under another gateway's id, or an encrypted packet, is not exempt.
- `docs/features/mqtt-setups.md` notes the exemption.

## Tests

- `okToMqtt.test.ts`: 3 new cases for `isOwnMapReport` (own report accepted; another gateway's, other portnums and encrypted packets rejected).
- `mqttBridgeManager.test.ts`: an end-to-end case with a real local and upstream broker. A firmware-shaped map report reaches the upstream broker, while a normal packet with the bit clear from the same node is still dropped (`uplinkOkToMqttDrops` = 1). Without the fix this test fails.
- `lint:ci` (ratchet) and `typecheck` pass.

Not tested against a live node on the public broker.

title: feat(config): pick a node's fixed position by dropping a pin on a map (Meshtastic + MeshCore)
body:
## Summary

Set a node's fixed position by dropping a pin on a map, the way **Set fixed position** works in the Meshtastic iOS app. It works on both protocols:

- **Meshtastic:** Configuration → Position. With **Fixed Position** on, a map appears under the Latitude / Longitude / Altitude fields.
- **MeshCore:** Configuration → Location. The map appears under the Latitude / Longitude fields.

On the map you can:

- **click** to drop a pin,
- **drag** the pin to move it,
- or press **Use this device's location** to put it where the browser says you are (the browser asks first).

The pin fills in the existing fields. Typing coordinates moves the pin, and the map pans to it if it's off screen. **Nothing is sent to the node until you press Save**, which uses the same save path as before:

- Meshtastic: `set_fixed_position` followed by `set_config.position`.
- MeshCore: `set_coords`.

![Fixed position map pin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maxhayim/meshmonitor/ced6c79a0/docs/public/images/features/fixed-position-map-pin.png)

## Details

- **New shared component** `src/components/map/LocationPinPicker.tsx`. It builds on `BaseMap` and uses a CSS-module pin drawn with theme tokens only. The helpers are in `locationPin.ts`.
- **"No position":** `(0, 0)` is what both firmwares report when a node has no position, so the picker treats it as no position and opens on a world view.
- **Precision:**
  - Meshtastic rounds to 7 decimals (`degrees * 1e7`); MeshCore rounds to 6 (`degrees * 1e6`).
  - Longitude is wrapped back into -180..180 when the map has been panned across the antimeridian.
- **Permissions:** the map follows each section's existing write gate. Without `configuration:write`, or when the MeshCore node is disconnected, it shows the position but ignores clicks and drags.
- **Docs:** `device.md` (Fixed Position, with a screenshot) and `meshcore.md` (Location).

## Mesh impact checklist

The picker sends no packets. It only changes form fields. Packets go out on Save, exactly as when you type the coordinates by hand: one admin message pair for Meshtastic, or one `set_coords` for MeshCore. There are no new timers, notifications or automation paths.

## Testing

- **`LocationPinPicker.test.tsx` (11 tests):**
  - "no position" handling, rounding and longitude wrap;
  - click to place, drag to move, disabled state;
  - panning to the pin when it is off screen;
  - browser location, both allowed and refused.
- **`PositionConfigSection.mapPin.test.tsx` (4 tests):**
  - no map while Fixed Position is off;
  - a pin fills the latitude and longitude fields;
  - locked without write access.
- **`MeshCoreConfigurationView.mapPin.test.tsx` (3 tests):**
  - a pin fills the fields and Save location calls `setCoords` with them, and nothing is sent before Save;
  - locked when disconnected or read-only.

title: feat(virtual-node): replay missed text messages when a client reconnects (#6160)
body:
## What

When a phone app reconnects to a Virtual Node, re-send the text messages stored while it was asleep. Android freezes the Meshtastic app in the background and MeshMonitor drops idle VN clients after 5 minutes, so messages stored meanwhile never reach the app — channels and DMs show a gap. A real node keeps a per-client queue; the VN has the database, so it does the same.

After the config handshake the VN waits a short settle delay (so a follow-up `want_config` doesn't trigger a double replay), then re-sends stored text messages since the app's last sign of life. Each goes out with its **original packet id and sender**, so the app's own dedup absorbs the overlap. **No LoRa airtime** — replay only travels the local TCP link to the app.

Scope is **replay only**; the companion fixes (#6161–#6164) are tracked separately (#6162/#6164 already merged). `pki_encrypted` for live sends comes from #6166.

## Confirmed limits (@framortej)

- **50 ms** pacing between messages
- **2000** messages per connection, keeping the **newest**
- **24 h** window on first connect (no mark yet)
- re-send from **lastSeen − 10 min** (overlap margin)
- **~3 s** settle delay after `config_complete`; a follow-up config resets it
- **OPT-IN** (off by default) for this first release

## Last-seen mark

The mark is the time of the last packet received *from* a replay-target client, **shared across all target clients** (one phone shows up on LAN/VPN with different IPs), persisted per source under the settings key `virtualNode.replayLastSeen.<sourceId>` (write throttled ~60 s, survives restarts). It does **not** move on a client's own writes until that client's replay is done, and **never** moves if a client leaves mid-replay — so the next connect replays the whole set again. Loopback and an excluded-IP list are never targets and never move the mark.

## Filtering

Only portnum-1 text (reactions `emoji` and replies `replyId` included). MeshMonitor's internal notes (ids without an underscore) and the app's own sends (`sourcePath === 'tcp_radio'` from the local node) are skipped. DMs only when they involve the local node.

## Per-peer `pki_encrypted` recomputation

The replay rebuilds each packet from the stored row, and #6166 only set `pki_encrypted` on the live broadcast copy — so it is recomputed here: a DM involving the local node whose peer has a public key and **no** key mismatch, cached per peer for the run. Without it Android files replayed DMs under channel 0 (#6162).

## Settings / UI

New global opt-in toggle `virtualNodeReplayEnabled` and typed exclude list `virtualNodeReplayExcludeIps` (added to `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS` + `GLOBAL_ONLY_SETTINGS_KEYS`; the `VN_REPLAY_EXCLUDE_IPS` env var remains a fallback), wired into a new **"Virtual Node message replay"** global Settings section via the SettingsDraft/handleSave Category-C pattern.

## Mesh impact

No LoRa airtime (local TCP only). The one risk is a phone notification storm, bounded by the 50 ms pacing + 2000 cap —

title: feat(meshtastic): decode and show DeviceMetadata.ble_address (#6157)
body:
## What

Meshtastic firmware `develop` now populates a new `DeviceMetadata` field, `ble_address` (protobufs#1159) — the BLE MAC a node advertises, e.g. `"AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"`. Our `protobufs` submodule predated it. This decodes the field and surfaces it for the local node and for remote nodes whose metadata we already fetch. Empty/absent = unknown (shown as nothing).

Closes #6157

## Submodule bump

- `protobufs`: `2542e06` (v2.8.0-130) → `b7fde64` (master tip).
- The field landed upstream in commit `6e9daf9` ("Add DeviceMetadata.ble_address (#1159)"); `b7fde64` carries `string ble_address = 17;` in `DeviceMetadata` (`meshtastic/mesh.proto`).
- Forward-only but wide: the bump pulls in ~40 additive upstream proto commits across mesh/config/module_config/etc. These are additive field changes that protobufjs tolerates. **Submodule pin only — no `.proto` file was hand-edited.** The full test suite + PG/MySQL in CI is the regression authority for the bump.

## Decode → route → UI path

- **Server decode/store** (`meshtasticManager.ts`): `processDeviceMetadata()` reads `metadata.bleAddress` (protobufjs camelCases `ble_address`), treats an empty string as absent (`undefined`), and stores it on the local-node metadata state and `getLocalNodeInfo()`. Remote nodes already store the full decoded `getDeviceMetadataResponse`, so `bleAddress` rides along.
- **Routes** (include only when non-empty): `configRoutes` (reads it from the live manager, since it is not persisted to the `nodes` row), `pollRoutes`, and the admin `get-device-metadata` route (local + remote branches).
- **Frontend**: `InfoTab` shows a "BLE Address" line for the local node; the `AdminCommandsTab` Device Metadata block shows a "BLE Address" row (which also covers remote nodes once their metadata loads). Both guard on a non-empty string. New **flat** i18n keys (`info.ble_address`, `admin_commands.ble_address`) in `public/locales/en.json`; no hardcoded colors (uses `var(--color-*)`).

## Virtual Node

The VN server relays raw frames and only decodes admin messages to intercept specific ops; `DeviceMetadata` responses pass through as raw bytes for client-side decode. So the field passes through unchanged once protobufs is bumped — there is no server-side VN metadata transform to extend and no dedicated VN metadata test seam.

## Firmware availability

Firmware-`develop`-only today. Current releases send an empty string for `ble_address`, which is shown as unknown (nothing).

## Tests

- `meshtasticManager.bleAddress.test.ts` (new): `processDeviceMetadata` stores `bleAddress` when present, leaves it undefined for empty string and for older firmware.
- `adminRoutes.deviceActions.test.ts`: get-device-metadata includes `bleAddress` when present, omits for empty/absent (local node).
- `configRoutes.test.ts`: `/config` includes the manager's `bleAddress` when advertised, omits otherwise.
- `pollRoutes.scope.test.ts`: `/poll` config carries `bleAddress` for a source that advertises one, omits for a s

title: feat(meshtastic): free-form remote-admin CLI console (#6154)
body:
## Summary

Gives Meshtastic remote admin a free-form CLI console with an output view, mirroring the existing MeshCore console. The operator types only the CLI arguments; the UI shows the fixed prefix `meshtastic --dest !xxxxxxxx` and renders the command output.

Closes #6154

## Design

**Transport (VN-only).** Commands relay through that source's **Virtual Node** — exactly how `examples/auto-responder-scripts/remote-admin.sh` works via `MESHTASTIC_IP`/`MESHTASTIC_PORT`. The VN host/port is resolved from the source's own manager: new `MeshtasticManager.getVirtualNodeTarget()` returns `{ host: '127.0.0.1', port }` from the running `VirtualNodeServer` (new `getPort()`), or `null` when the VN is disabled. When disabled, the route refuses with **409 `VIRTUAL_NODE_DISABLED`** instead of falling back to the physical radio (which would kill MeshMonitor's own link). Argv is built as `[--host <vnHost>, --port <vnPort>, --dest, !xxxxxxxx, ...userArgs]`.

**Backend route.** New source-scoped `POST /api/sources/:id/meshtastic/admin/cli` (`meshtasticAdminRoutes`, mounted at `/api/sources/:id/meshtastic`). Gated on `requireAuth()` + `requirePermission('remote_admin','write',{ sourceIdFrom: 'params.id' })` + a new `meshtasticDeviceLimiter`, with `extendRequestTimeout`. Uses the `ok`/`fail` envelope. Validates the `--dest` id (`!xxxxxxxx`). Captures stdout+stderr; maps timeout → **504 `CLI_TIMEOUT`**, non-zero exit → **422 `CLI_NONZERO_EXIT`** (both carry the output), spawn failure → **502 `CLI_RUN_FAILED`**, non-Meshtastic source → **400 `SOURCE_NOT_MESHTASTIC`**. Audited via `auditLogAsync` with secret values redacted.

**Frontend.** `MeshtasticRemoteCliConsole` reuses the shared `CliConsoleBody` primitive (typed-name danger modal) and is added as a section in `AdminCommandsTab`, remote-only and disabled when the VN/node is unavailable. New i18n strings added to `public/locales/en.json` as flat keys.

## 🔒 Security note (deliberate maintainer decision)

**Full pass-through of CLI flags, no allowlist.** This was an explicit maintainer decision: flags like `--export-config`, `--configure`, `--host`, `--port` are reachable. The risk is accepted in exchange for the full power of the `meshtastic` CLI. Mitigations in place:

- **No shell, ever.** The free-form string is split by a quote-aware splitter (`parseCliArgs`, no shell, capped length + arg count) and run with `execFile` and an argv **array**. User input is never interpolated into a command string, so `;`, `|`, `&&`, `$()` are inert literal tokens. Timeout kills the child.
- **Remote only.** Every invocation targets `--dest`; no local-node mode.
- **Typed-name danger confirmation.** `--reboot`/`--factory-reset`/`--shutdown` (and similar) require `confirm:true`, enforced **server-side** (mirrors the MeshCore `DANGER_COMMAND_PATTERN` guard) so a script or direct API call cannot bypass the frontend modal.
- **Permission-gated per source** (`remote_admin:write`, `sourceIdFrom`) and rate-limited.
- **VN-only tran

title: feat(meshtastic): send add_contact before set_favorite_node so remote favorites stick (#6153)
body:
## Summary

`set_favorite_node` is a no-op when the target radio does not hold the favorited node in its NodeDB, yet the radio still ACKs — so MeshMonitor recorded a false success. This implements the refined plan from issue #6153.

Before sending `set_favorite_node`, MeshMonitor now sends an `add_contact` (AddContact admin message) built from the node's stored user data. The firmware's `addFromContact` creates the NodeDB entry **and**, for most device roles, sets the favorite flag in the same step.

### Role-based follow-up logic

The follow-up `set_favorite_node` is sent **only** when:
- the administered (destination) radio's role is `CLIENT_BASE` — firmware deliberately skips the favorite inside `addFromContact` (`NodeDB.cpp:3848-3853`), or
- the destination role is **unknown** to MeshMonitor (we can't assume `add_contact` set it).

For every other known role, `add_contact` alone sets the favorite, so the extra `set_favorite_node` packet is skipped. This means **one extra admin packet only on CLIENT_BASE / unknown targets** — other known roles cost the same single packet as before.

### Safety

- If MeshMonitor holds essentially no user data for the node (no long name, short name, or public key), `add_contact` is skipped and it falls back to today's behavior (`set_favorite_node` only) rather than sending an empty contact that would clobber the target's fresher fields.
- If `add_contact` throws, a warning is logged and `set_favorite_node` is still sent — favorites never get worse than today.
- The removal path (`sendRemoveFavoriteNode`) is **not** touched.

## Changes

- `src/server/protobufService.ts` — `createAddContactMessage` gains an optional trailing `sessionPasskey?: Uint8Array`, attached on the AdminMessage (not inside the addContact payload), mirroring `createSetFavoriteNodeMessage`. Remote targets reject state-changing admin messages without the session passkey.
- `src/server/services/favoritesService.ts` — centralized the add_contact-first behavior inside `sendFavoriteNode` (fire-and-forget add_contact) and `sendFavoriteNodeAwaitAck` (awaits the add_contact ACK before the follow-up; returns the add_contact ACK when the follow-up is skipped, so the public return shape is unchanged). Node data read through the nodes repository scoped to `sourceId`; `CLIENT_BASE` resolved via the shared `DeviceRole` enum (no magic number).

title: feat(meshcore): Rooms list sort dropdown + custom order, and click-to-deselect (#6148, #6149)
body:
## Summary

Two related MeshCore Rooms-view changes (both touch `MeshCoreRoomsView.tsx`, so one PR), each mirroring existing Channels-page behavior.

### #6148 — Rooms list sort dropdown + Custom order
Adds a display-only sort control to the Rooms list, modeled on the Channels page (#5385/#5379/#5503):
- **Room name** (default, stable) — alphabetical by shown name (`advName` → `name` → key prefix).
- **Last message** — newest sender-time post first (`m.timestamp`, not receipt time, so a login backlog replay does not jump a room to the top, #5973); no-post rooms sink.
- **Message count** — busiest first; empty rooms sink.
- **Distance** — nearest first from the source node to each room; 0/0 and absent coords count as "no location" (`advertHasPosition`) and sink, ordered by name. Disabled when the source node has no fix (falls back to Room name).
- **Custom** — drag-and-drop order via the shared reorder list.

Count and last-message values are computed once per render (no per-comparison re-filter). Mode + custom order persist **per source** in `localStorage` (`meshmonitor-meshcore-room-*`), so a read-only viewer sorts without `settings:write`. A room that joins after a custom order was saved is appended deterministically; a stale saved key is ignored.

**Helper generalization (kept Channels working):** `meshcoreChannelOrder.ts` now has an `OrderKey = string | number` generic engine — `sortItems`, `applyCustomOrder`, and the tie-break `compareKey` work for both integer channel slots and room `publicKey` strings. `sortChannels` is a thin alias of `sortItems`; `OrderableChannel`/`SortChannelsOptions` remain as aliases. `MeshCoreChannelReorderList` is now a generic component (`K extends OrderKey`, default `number`), so the channel call site is unchanged and rooms pass string ids (dnd-kit's `UniqueIdentifier` already covers both). Added `RoomSortMode` + room persistence (default `name`; no channel-only `device` mode).

### #6149 — click the selected Room Server to de-select
A desktop click on the already-open room de-selects it and returns to the landing pane, mirroring the Channels toggle (#6049/#6112). **Mobile** keeps reopening the room (the list is the landing view and Back leaves `selectedRoom` set). De-select clears the login/sync form state (same as a normal select) but **keeps `loggedInRooms`** (view change, not a logout) and **skips `loadSyncConfig`** (no selected room).

## Mesh impact
Display / view-state only — no packets, no transmission, no timers. No rate limits needed.

## Tests
- Extended `meshcoreChannelOrder.test.ts` with string-key (room) cases for every mode, room persistence (per-source, default name, sanitization), distinct storage keys, and the `sortChannels === sortItems` alias.
- New `MeshCoreRoomsView.sort.test.tsx`: each mode's order incl. sink rules, distance with/without a source fix (option disabled), per-source mode persistence, and a new room appended under a saved custom order.
- New `MeshCoreRoomsView.deselect.test.tsx

body:
## Summary

Adds a `discover.neighbors` quick-action button to the MeshCore Remote Admin command sections, as requested in #3351.

- **Remote Admin console** (`MeshCoreRemoteConsole`): new `discover_neighbors` entry in `REMOTE_ACTION_CATALOG`, shown only for Repeaters via a new `isRepeater` prop (passed as `advType === 2` from `MeshCoreContactDetailPanel`).
- **Directly-attached repeater console** (`MeshCoreLocalConsole`): same entry in `REPEATER_ACTION_CATALOG`, dropped for Room Servers (`deviceType !== 2`) since the catalog is shared by deviceType 2 and 3.

`discover.neighbors` is `simple_repeater`-only firmware (companion-v1.14.0+), so it appears for **Repeaters only** (advType/deviceType === 2) and is **hidden for Room Servers** (=== 3).

Closes #3351

## Mesh impact

- The command triggers a **zero-hop** neighbor discovery — the same airtime class as the existing `advert` quick action, so no new rate limit is introduced (it mirrors `advert` exactly).

- Because it transmits, it carries the same **receive-only gating** as `advert`: the remote console body is already blocked under receive-only, and the local action is disabled (not removed, so the user still learns it exists) with the receive-only tooltip.

title: feat(reticulum): send and reply over Reticulum from the Automation Engine (#6143)
body:
Closes #6143

## Summary

Reticulum (LXMF) **inbound** already fired the "A message is received" trigger; **outbound** was
broken. `sendTextVia` handed `ReticulumManager.sendMessage` a bare positional string (it wants a
`{ to, content }` object, and it *also* has a `sendMessage` method, so the MeshCore duck-typed
branch swallowed Reticulum targets), and the DM target was coerced through `num()`, so an LXMF hash
came out `NaN` and was lost.

This PR makes Reticulum a first-class send/reply target in the Automation Engine.

## What was implemented (section 3)

1. **`sendTextVia` Reticulum branch** (`meshActionDeps.ts`) — checked via `isReticulumManager`
   **before** the MeshCore branch, and calls `sendMessage({ to, content, replyToHash? })` (object
   form).
2. **DM target as a string hash** (`actionExecutor.ts`) — a Reticulum send resolves `to` with
   `str()`, never `num()`, so `{{ trigger.from }}` replies to the sender.
3. **"Reply to the triggering message" → `replyToHash`** — the triggering LXMF message's own hash
   is exposed on the context as `messageHash` (`triggerContext.ts`) and mapped to the outgoing
   `replyToHash`.
4. **No destination → recorded skip** — LXMF has no channels, so there is no broadcast fallback; a
   Reticulum send with no resolvable `to` records `{ skipped: true, reason: … }` rather than
   throwing or guessing.
5. **Failure semantics** — not-connected / send-rejected throws, which the executor surfaces as a
   failed step (mirrors MeshCore).
6. **"On channels" ignored** for a Reticulum target.
7. **Meshtastic/MeshCore-only actions on Reticulum → recorded skip** — tapback, node manage, request
   data, device reboot. New `isReticulumSource` helper (mirrors `isMeshCoreSource`).
8. **Tokens** — `fromName`/`senderLabel` filled from the announced destination `displayName`
   (new `getReticulumDisplayName` data-provider method → `reticulum.getDestination`), with the raw
   LXMF hash as fallback.
9. **Builder** — RET badge (`protoBadge`), RET badge colour via `var(--chart-4)` (CSS token, no
   hex), and `sourceMatchesProtocol` now treats Reticulum as its own protocol (a Meshtastic-only
   field no longer offers a Reticulum source; `isSendableSource` keeps Reticulum sendable).
   `sourceProtocol('reticulum')` returns `'reticulum'` so the whole send loop stays uniform.
10. **SubstitutionsHelp** — Reticulum-only tokens (`title`, `quality`, `method`,
    `signatureValidated`, `ratcheted`, `replyToHash`, `threadHash`) and `reticulum`/`RET` added to
    the `protocol`/`protocolShort` descriptions.
11. **Docs** — new "Reticulum (LXMF) support" section in `docs/features/automation-engine.md`
    (trigger support, the filter limits, the token list + always-blank fields, send/reply/skip
    behaviour), and corrected the "Send via sources", "On channels", "DM to node #" and "Reply to
    the triggering message" entries.

## Decisions

**No Reticulum-specific "announce" action in this PR.** `ReticulumManager.announceNow()` exists, but

title: fix(meshtastic): default lora.txEnabled to false when a device config omits it (#6142)
body:
Closes #6142

## Problem
A receive-only Meshtastic radio (`lora.tx_enabled=false`) sends a config where proto3 omits the false `txEnabled`. The server never backfilled it, so `deviceStatusRoutes` (`!== false`), `sourceRoutes` (`?? true`) and `isTxEnabled()` all read `true`. The Device Config UI showed Transmit Enabled on, and a LoRa save shipped `txEnabled:true` — re-enabling TX on a node meant to be receive-only, defeating #4294 and un-gating autonomous senders after a reconnect.

## Fix
Backfill `txEnabled=false` in both default passes in `meshtasticManager.ts` (the config-receive pass and `loraConfigWithDefaults`) whenever the `lora` block is present but omits `txEnabled`. The fail-open `true` is kept in the readers for the genuine "no config has arrived yet" case.

## Tests
Regression tests: a decoded config that omits `txEnabled` now stores/returns `false`; an explicit `true` is preserved.

Related: #4294, #4308, #4315.

title: build(deps): bump croner from 10.0.1 to 11.0.0
body:
Bumps [croner](https://github.com/Hexagon/croner) from 10.0.1 to 11.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from croner's releases.

11.0.0

Croner 11.0.0 is a major release focused on correctness and predictability: DST handling aligned with croner-rust and Vixie cron, a new iterator API, and a long list of scheduling fixes around timezones, clock changes and edge-case patterns.

Highlights

  • Iterator API — The new enumerate() method returns a stateful CronIterator that works with for...of, destructuring, next(), peek() and reset(), and honors maxRuns.

  • Predictable DST handling — DST transitions now work as in croner-rust and Vixie cron. Fixed-time jobs in a spring-forward gap run at the first valid time after it, and interval jobs keep running through the repeated hour at fall back. Negative timer re-arming during fall back is fixed.

  • Inclusive startAt — A pattern match exactly at startAt now runs.

  • dayOffset that matches reality — nextRun(), nextRuns(), previousRuns(), msToNext() and enumerate() return actual run times, the same ones the scheduler uses.

  • Date-based jobs for "now" — A one-off job dated up to 1 second in the past fires immediately. The new allowPast option lets older dates fire too.

  • Faster timezone scheduling — Intl.DateTimeFormat instances are cached per timezone.

  • Timezone and clock robustness — ISO 8601 strings are read in the job's timezone/utcOffset, and scheduling recovers properly after system clock steps forward or backward.

Breaking Changes

  • DST handling aligned with croner-rust and Vixie cron, deliberately deviating from OCPS 1.4 §4.3.1 (0 30 2 * * * in a DST gap now runs at 3:00 AM instead of 3:30 AM, and interval jobs run on both occurrences of a repeated time)
  • startAt is inclusive (not when interval is set)
  • With dayOffset, nextRun() and related methods return actual run times, and startAt/stopAt apply to the shifted run time
  • previousRun() returns when the previous run started, as documented, instead of when it finished

See the migration guide further down for a smooth upgrade from 10.x.

Thank you to all contributors, and a special welcome to @​SynthLuvr

title: build(deps): bump react-i18next from 17.0.18 to 17.1.9
body:
Bumps [react-i18next](https://github.com/i18next/react-i18next) from 17.0.18 to 17.1.9.
Changelog

Sourced from react-i18next's changelog.

17.1.9

  • fix(useTranslation): namespaces added to or removed from the ns array are now picked up. The hook used the array itself as the useMemo dependency list, and React only compares the entries both lists have in common when its length changes, so going from useTranslation(['nsA']) to useTranslation(['nsA', 'nsB']) kept returning ['nsA']: React warned that the dependency array changed size, nsB was never loaded, and with nsMode: 'fallback' keys only in nsB rendered as the key. Removing a namespace kept the old list the same way. The namespaces are now compared by content, so a growing list loads the new namespace (suspending until it is loaded, as switching from 'nsA' to 'nsB' already does) and t uses it. Lists that keep their length behave as before. Thanks @​lprnmns (#1945).

17.1.8

  • fix(Trans): an interpolation variable named format is no longer dropped. Trans reads format in an interpolation object as the formatter name ({{ value, format }}), so with {{ format }} as the only key nothing was left: <Trans>Export as {{ format }}</Trans> warned TRANS_INVALID_OBJ and used the default string Export as instead of Export as {{format}}. When format is the object's only key it is now treated as the variable. {{ value, format }} works as before. Without an i18nKey, the key derived from the children changes accordingly, from Export as to Export as {{format}}. i18next-cli serializes Trans children with react-i18next, so extracting with this version produces the same key. Thanks @​Pharex38 (#1944).

17.1.7

  • fix(IcuTrans): each HTML entity in a translation is now decoded exactly once. Named, decimal and hexadecimal entities were decoded in three passes, and each pass decoded the output of the previous one, so an escaped numeric entity was decoded twice: "Write &[#169](https://github.com/i18next/react-i18next/issues/169); to get &[#169](https://github.com/i18next/react-i18next/issues/169);" rendered Write © to get © instead of Write &[#169](https://github.com/i1

title: feat(reticulum): RNode interface status on Info page + battery/Ch/Air header (#6120)
body:
## What

Implements #6120: surface the live RNode interface status on the Reticulum **Info** page, and show **battery + `Ch x% · Air y%`** in the per-source header, mirroring the Meshtastic header.

RNS already returns these from `Reticulum.get_interface_stats()` for an RNode LoRa interface (`airtime_short/long`, `channel_load_short/long`, `noise_floor`, `interference` + `interference_last_ts/dbm`, `cpu_load`, `battery_state`, `battery_percent`), but the bridge dropped them and `reticulum_interfaces` had no columns.

## Bridge decision: in-tree

`bridge/` is a **plain in-tree directory** in this repo (tracked by git; only `protobufs` and `takpacket-sdk` are submodules). So the bridge change ships **in this PR** — no follow-up needed. `_normalize_interface()` now passes the extra fields through, null when absent (non-RNode interfaces report none).

## Changes

- **Bridge** (`rns_manager.py`): `_normalize_interface()` relays the 11 extra fields (null when absent). Units are left exactly as RNS/`rnstatus` present them — airtime/channel-load/cpu-load are percentages, noise-floor/interference are dBm, `interference_last_ts` is RNS epoch **seconds** — no scaling.
- **Schema + migration 221**: 11 nullable columns on `reticulum_interfaces` for all three backends (SQLite/PG/MySQL), idempotent via the shared helpers; registered in `src/db/migrations.ts`. Hand-written PG/MySQL `CREATE TABLE` DDL in `reticulum.test.ts` updated too.
- **Persist + relay**: `upsertInterface` writes them each poll; `InterfaceStatsEntry` + `reticulumManager.handleInterfaceStats` carry them; `GET /api/sources/:id/reticulum/interfaces` already returns the full row.
- **Info page**: new **Interface status** card — one block per interface that reports a gauge, hiding rows with no value and the whole section when nothing reports.
- **Header**: `ReticulumSourcePage` reuses the existing `CyclingConnectionStatus` (the Meshtastic header display), fed by the **first Up RNode interface** via `reticulumHeaderMetrics()`. Values hide entirely when no Up RNode interface reports them.

## Scope guard (does NOT touch #6121)

Display-only. The interface **count** / **online** semantics (`interfaceCount`, row pruning) are untouched — those belong to #6121 (@temalo). No row deletion, no count changes.

## Tests

- Route test (harness): `/interfaces` returns the new fields when present and null when absent.
- UI tests: Info card hides empty rows / hides the section when nothing reports; `reticulumHeaderMetrics` picks the first Up RNode and returns `undefined` when none report.
- Repository round-trip test; migration 221 SQLite + mocked PG/MySQL DDL test + PG/MySQL container round-trip test.
- Bridge unit test for the new `_normalize_interface` passthrough.

## Verification

- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` — 0 errors.
- Full Vitest — `success: true`, 33708 passed / 0 failed / 1823 skipped.
- `npm run lint:ci` (minus `.claude/worktrees` noise) — clean; CSS colour check OK.
- PG/MySQL container su
